procurementStages.name: Foundations
procurementStages.remember: Buying for our own needs means procurement: compete, disclose, refuse gifts.
keyFacts: value of gifts you may accept
procurementStages.example: A project team wants to pay an NGO to run its own awareness campaign that also promotes Council of Europe values. Because the NGO pursues its own objectives and only costs are covered, this is a grant, not procurement. The correct action is to use a grant agreement under Rule No. 1374, not a tender.
procurementStages.title: Principles, Legal Bases & Ethics
procurementStages.lead: Understand the rules that govern every Council of Europe purchase and the ethical standards expected of everyone involved. Confirm that procurement, not a grant, is the right instrument.
procurementStages.understand: Every purchase of works, goods or services to meet the Organisation's own needs is procurement and must follow one of the procedures in Rule No. 1395.
procurementStages.do: Check that the activity is a purchase rather than financial assistance, and apply the six procurement principles throughout the procedure.
procurementStages.check: Your annual declaration of interests is filed and no conflict of interest, gift or privileged contact with potential bidders exists.

sections.lead: Three instruments set the rules for every Council of Europe purchase, and DLAPIL templates replace the older model contracts.
items: Set out the three types of contract, the three main procedures and the role of the Tenders Board.
Details each procedure, from preparing the tender file to signing the contract. An annotated version is on the Tenders Board's web page.
Cover consultants' contracts and outsourcing contracts respectively and remain relevant as background.
must: Buyer entities should use the DLAPIL templates instead of the model contracts in Instructions No. 59 and No. 60, and should not use the model invoice.

sections.lead: Six principles from Rule No. 1395 guide every procurement procedure: competition is the norm and direct award the exception.
items: Competitive procedures are launched at regular intervals so that other suppliers also have the chance to compete.
The buyer entity acts without partiality, bias or outside influence, with neutral tender documents and impartial scoring.
Criteria and rules are available to all tenderers, results are published and reasons for the award are given on request.
The Council avoids recurring, exclusive relationships with suppliers and contracts of excessive length.
All tenderers follow the same rules and receive the same information at each stage.
Tenderers in a comparable situation are not treated differently because they belong to a particular group, especially in the conditions for taking part.

sections.lead: Buying for the Organisation's own needs is procurement; financing a grantee's own project is a grant.
items: Used whenever the Organisation buys works, goods or services for its own needs, whatever the contractor's status. The price includes a profit margin and there are no reporting requirements.

Used when the Organisation gives financial assistance to a grantee for the grantee's own project (Article 43 bis of the Financial Regulations and Rule No. 1374). It covers part of the grantee's costs and requires extensive reporting.

sections.lead: Everyone involved in procurement follows the Code of Conduct and the Purchasing Code of Ethics (25 October 2005), and the Council has a no-gift policy.
items: Do not take part in a procedure where your own interests could conflict with the Council's.
Do not disclose the content of offers.
Maintain professional, respectful and trusting relationships with suppliers.
Select suppliers on objective and impartial criteria.
Refuse any benefit, gift or solicitation from suppliers, whatever its value.
must: Secretariat members involved in procurement must submit a declaration of interests every year by the end of January, or within one month of a change (Rule No. 1282).

sections.lead: Suspected fraud, corruption or other wrongdoing is reported at once under the Speak Up Policy.
must: Staff must report suspected fraud, corruption or other wrongdoing immediately to the DIO.
Staff must not give potential bidders privileged technical or financial information before the call is public.
Buyer entities must not write specifications restrictively to discourage competition.

sections.lead: Four kinds of auditor examine procurement, and non-compliance creates institutional, financial, ethical, reputational and operational risks.
items: Internal audit checks compliance and performance.
Certifies the accounts and may carry out performance audits.
must: The Ordinary Budget must cover any ineligible expenditure that donors reclaim after a non-compliant procedure.
sections.tip: Auditors look at transparency, competition, thresholds, reasons for direct awards, validation workflows, declarations of interest and archiving, so keep these well documented.

procurementStages.warning: When non-compliant procedures are funded by extrabudgetary resources, the donor can declare the expenditure ineligible and demand a refund, which is then charged to the Ordinary Budget.
procurementStages.best: Use the procurement principles as a guiding thread at every stage. When in doubt on an ethics question, consult the Ethics Officer before contacting a supplier.
checklist: Confirm the activity is a purchase, not a grant
Identify the applicable rules: Financial Regulations Art. 40–43 and Rule No. 1395
Submit or update your declaration of interests
Refuse any gift or hospitality from suppliers
Report any suspicion of fraud to the DIO
Keep pre-launch information confidential from potential bidders

procurementStages.name: Roles & Funding
procurementStages.remember: Operations prepare, the CCM validates, the Tenders Board controls above €184,000.
procurementStages.example: A field office plans a €40,000 IT equipment purchase for a ministry under an EU-funded project. IT purchases need DIT approval. The correct action is to request permission via MSA 1002, check the budget line, and appoint authorised staff members in writing before launch.
procurementStages.title: Actors, Funding & Types of Purchases
procurementStages.lead: Know who prepares, validates, controls and supports each step, and how the funding source and type of purchase affect the procedure.
procurementStages.understand: Procurement is decentralised: each MAE buys for its own needs, keeping operational functions separate from validation and financial management functions.
procurementStages.do: Identify your CCM, appoint authorised staff members in writing and contact DLAPIL, the Procurement Unit or specialist directorates early.
procurementStages.check: Authorised staff members are designated in writing by the CO or CCM before they open or assess offers.

sections.lead: Each MAE runs its own procurement, with operational functions kept separate from validation and financial functions.
items: Defining needs, drafting tender documents and assessing deliverables.
Budgetary verification, PO validation and transfers.
must: Each MAE must ensure that the same person does not perform both operational and validation functions.
sections.tip: Roles follow the Financial Management Framework, the general delegation framework CM/Res(2023)1 and each MAE's delegations.

sections.lead: The buyer entity runs the whole process, from forecasting the need to executing the contract.
must: Only authorised staff members designated by the CO or CCM may open offers, assess offers and negotiate (Rule No. 1395, Article 3.2.d).
sections.tip: Delegate this authority in writing, at the latest when the CCM approves the tender documents, using the standard e-mail paragraph.

sections.lead: Four bodies control and validate procurement decisions.
items: Authorises expenditure and usually delegates to CCMs.
Validates the choice of procedure, tender files, awards and contracts, assisted by an ACCM and a FOMA.
Ensures compliance for all contracts above €184,000 excluding VAT, decides on the scope and publication of international calls and scrutinises bid analyses.

sections.lead: Four services support buyer entities with legal, practical, Board and payment matters.
items: Handles all legal questions, provides templates and training and, since 1 February 2025, performs the Legal Compliance Review for extrabudgetary-funded procedures between €55,000 and €184,000.
Gives non-legal support such as market analysis, sourcing, e-procurement and analysis tables, answering within 48 hours at procurement@coe.int.
Checks files before they go to the Board.
Registers suppliers in FIMS and pays invoices.

sections.lead: Procurement is funded either from the Ordinary Budget or from extrabudgetary resources.
items: Come from the four-year Programme and Budget with a biennial cycle; procurement is planned on forecasts per budget line approved by the CO.
Include EU funds under joint programmes and voluntary contributions, earmarked or non-earmarked, including the Human Rights Trust Fund.
must: In co-operation projects, procurement must match the approved description of the action and budget, which can be difficult to amend.

sections.lead: Some types of purchase carry specific rules or need approval from a specialist directorate.
items: Knowledge-based, non-recurrent creations of the mind that always raise intellectual property issues.
Purchases need DIT approval (MSA 1002), and cloud deliverables require the Cloud Checklist.
Booked directly for participants, they are outside Rule No. 1395 (Article 7); bought through an agency, they are not.
must: Buyer entities must avoid disguised employment, for example by not giving consultants full-time or part-time workloads, CoE e-mail addresses or equipment.

sections.lead: Suppliers declare their use of AI, and co-operation projects follow specific planning roles.
must: Suppliers must declare any use of AI in the DLAPIL AI questionnaire, which is saved with the file.
Any difference between national and international consultants may only be based on expertise or language skills, never on nationality or residence.
items: Prepare forecasts that the CCM validates.

procurementStages.warning: Authority for authorised staff members must be delegated in writing by the CO or CCM before any opening, assessment or negotiation task is performed.
procurementStages.best: Check with the DPC or the Procurement Unit whether a framework contract or framework agreement already covers events, translation, interpretation, transport or printing in the country concerned.
checklist: Identify the CO/CCM responsible for the purchase
Designate authorised staff members in writing
Confirm the funding source: Ordinary Budget or extrabudgetary
Check the purchase matches the approved project budget lines
Obtain DIT, DC or DGS approval where the category requires it
Plan the AI questionnaire for intellectual deliverables

procurementStages.name: Market & Suppliers
procurementStages.remember: Source widely, share nothing in advance.
keyFacts: CEI is not a procurement procedure
procurementStages.example: A team always invites the same three consultants for gender-equality training. Auditors would see this as a breach of periodic competition. The correct action is to publish a call for expressions of interest and use the shortlist it produces for the next call for tenders.
procurementStages.title: Market Analysis & Supplier Sourcing
procurementStages.lead: Study the market and identify capable suppliers before drafting the tender, so that the call attracts enough good-quality offers.
procurementStages.understand: Market analysis and sourcing increase competition, reveal innovative solutions and risks, and support periodic competition and non-discrimination.
procurementStages.do: Use internal and external sources, existing contracts, the suppliers database and, where useful, a call for expressions of interest.
procurementStages.check: No potential bidder has received information that would give them an advantage in the future procedure.

sections.lead: A market analysis is essential when the goods, services or works have not been bought before.
items: Identifies suppliers beyond the usual ones.
Helps tender documents match what the market offers.
Brings out alternative or innovative proposals.
Shows what could go wrong or be improved.
sections.tip: Analyse the market before a direct award too, to check that better suppliers or solutions are not available.

sections.lead: Use sources that match the type of purchase, plus the Council's own records.
items: Trade journals, chambers of commerce, embassies, catalogues and end users.
Academic platforms such as researchgate.net, academia.edu and scholar.google.com, specialised journals, professional associations and LinkedIn.
Existing contracts lists, previous lists of invitees and market studies supported by the Procurement Unit.

sections.lead: A good strategy produces diverse offers, a proportionate workload and the best value for money.
items: Divide the contract into lots to widen competition.
Share existing contracts with other entities.
must: Buyer entities must make sure that SMEs and not-for-profit, minority-owned, women-owned and disability-inclusive suppliers are not excluded.

sections.lead: FIMS holds over 50,000 suppliers but few new ones are added, so the same suppliers often bid.
must: In a competitive bidding procedure, the buyer entity must invite at least three suppliers (Rule No. 1395, Article 21.2).
sections.tip: Choose the invitees through targeted sourcing, not a passive internet search, so that you receive three good-quality bids rather than just meeting the rule.

sections.lead: A CEI (Rule No. 1395, Article 5) is not a procurement procedure but a tool to list potential suppliers for future procedures.
items: The CoE website, e-procurement, the OJEU or social networks.
There is no need to invite every listed supplier or to justify not inviting someone.
There is no need to launch a call afterwards.
sections.tip: External auditors strongly recommend CEIs for consultancy.

sections.lead: The Procurement Unit's intranet holds an optional shared suppliers database by category, approved by the Data Protection Officer.
must: Registering a contracted supplier in FIMS requires an MSA 4002 processed by TPA.
sections.tip: The Council does not use blocklists, but an optional exclusion criterion covers suppliers who failed contractual obligations with the Council in the previous three years.

procurementStages.warning: When meeting potential suppliers, never share information about a future call for tenders that could give them an advantage. Consult DLAPIL or the Procurement Unit if in doubt.
procurementStages.best: Carry out the market study first and then the CEI, and include the CEI's results in the market study. The Procurement Unit can also consult the NPIO network of 40+ international organisations.
checklist: Check the framework contracts and agreements database for an existing contract
Consult internal and external market sources
Consider lots or a framework contract in your strategy
Launch a call for expressions of interest where useful
Search the suppliers database by category
Record why invited suppliers are relevant to the need

procurementStages.name: Define the Need
procurementStages.remember: Plan backwards from the deadline; one procedure per type of need.
procurementStages.example: A project expects 12 expert reports over its three-year life. Buying them one at a time would artificially split the need. The correct action is to estimate all 12 reports over the full project duration, including possible extensions, and run a single procedure.
procurementStages.title: Define & Group Procurement Needs
procurementStages.lead: Anticipate and describe the need precisely over the whole period of reference, grouping similar needs into as few procedures as possible.
procurementStages.understand: A clearly defined need over the correct period of reference determines the type of contract, the threshold and the procedure.
procurementStages.do: Plan backwards from the delivery date, group similar needs for the whole project or budget cycle, and consult the relevant in-house experts.
procurementStages.check: All foreseeable similar needs for the period of reference are covered, ideally by one procedure per type of need.

sections.lead: Identify needs as early as possible and build a reverse schedule from the required completion date.
items: Allow time for the Board to authorise the launch and the results.
Allow at least three weeks for international calls.
Allow time for the exemption procedures.
sections.tip: A procedure may be launched before the project formally starts if the tender documents state that the contract will only be awarded once it begins.

sections.lead: Answer a set of questions about the need before drafting anything.
items: What is expected and how often is it needed?
What is the estimated overall budget and which threshold applies?
Does an existing transversal contract already cover the need?
Payment terms, delivery time, penalties and language.
Consider the whole cost, not only the purchase price.

sections.lead: Specialist directorates confirm the need is not already covered in-house and help validate the approach.
must: The buyer entity must consult the relevant directorate before tendering.

sections.lead: Co-operation projects can buy project by project or for a whole sector.
items: Covers the needs of one project for its full duration, including possible extensions.
Covers common needs of several projects or a sector; it requires a framework contract or agreement and an international public call for tenders.
must: Under a sector-based approach, each order or call-off must be issued within one project, and the relevant CCMs must be consulted during drafting and informed of the results before any order is placed.

sections.lead: For Ordinary Budget purchases, consider the whole two-year budget cycle and cover similar needs with a minimum number of procedures.
must: Buyer entities must not repeat one-off purchases to meet a structural need.
sections.tip: Ad hoc procedures for unforeseeable needs remain possible.

procurementStages.warning: Last-minute purchases can only be justified in exceptional circumstances where the urgency is not attributable to the buyer entity.
procurementStages.best: Use a reverse schedule, working back from the completion date, to set milestones and a realistic start date for the procedure.
checklist: Describe the expected deliverables and frequency
Set the period of reference (project or budget cycle)
Choose project-based or sector-based approach
Estimate the total budget for all similar needs
Consult DGS, DIT, DC or ITEM where relevant
Build a reverse schedule including approvals and VAT steps

procurementStages.name: Contract Types
procurementStages.remember: Fixed need: one-off. Repeating units: framework contract. Variable: framework agreement.
keyFacts: minimum suppliers per framework agreement lot
procurementStages.example: A project needs a cybercrime trainer repeatedly, in one-hour, half-day and full-day formats, in Strasbourg or online. The volume is unknown but the units can be defined. The correct action is a framework contract with a price list per format and a pooling system for consultants.
procurementStages.title: One-off, Framework Contract or Framework Agreement
procurementStages.lead: Choose the contract type that matches how well defined and how repetitive the need is. The contract type does not determine the procedure.
procurementStages.understand: Use a one-off contract for defined, non-recurring needs, a framework contract for recurring unit-based needs, and a framework agreement for variable or complex needs.
procurementStages.do: Match the need to the contract type and decide the ordering system (ranking or pooling) or the call-off rules before launch.
procurementStages.check: The contract type fits the need, its duration does not exceed four years (five exceptionally), and it does not overlap existing contracts.

sections.lead: A contract is not a procedure: the procedure depends on value, while the type of contract depends on the need.
items: Use when the need is quantifiable, definable and very unlikely to recur. One supplier (possibly a consortium); no orders, as price, specifications and quantities are fixed; lasts until both parties complete their obligations and cannot be renewed; control: a delivery deadline per deliverable, signed by the CCM.

Use when the need can be defined as units and recurs often but cannot be fully quantified. One supplier (simple) or several (multiple, ranked or pooled); the buyer entity issues order forms at fixed unit prices; maximum four years, five exceptionally; control: the CCM signs each order after the PO is raised.

Use when the need is regular but variable, uncertain or complex. At least three suppliers per lot; each need goes to a call-off (mini-competition) approved by the CCM; maximum four years, five exceptionally; control: the CCM signs each call-off, and call-offs above €184,000 go to the Tenders Board.

sections.lead: A one-off contract is made with a single supplier, possibly a consortium, and may be split into lots.
must: A one-off contract must define the price, specifications and quantities.
A one-off contract must state a delivery deadline for each deliverable and cannot be renewed.
Buyer entities must not use repeated one-off contracts for the same need, as this is prohibited artificial splitting.
sections.tip: A one-off contract lasts until both parties have completed their obligations.

sections.lead: A framework contract fixes unit prices for defined items or time-based units, and the Council is not obliged to buy.
items: Orders go to suppliers in ranked order; recommended for goods and general services.
The buyer chooses a supplier for each order, justified in a note approved by the CCM; better for intellectual services.
must: A multiple framework contract tender must state whether ranking or pooling applies.
Under a framework contract, only listed items can be ordered, and no order can be created after the end date.

sections.lead: A framework agreement creates a pool of at least three suppliers per lot, selected on competence without price competition.
items: Choose at least three suppliers per lot on competence.
The CCM approves each call-off before publication.
Each need is put out to a call-off among the pool.
must: Any call-off with a single value above €184,000 must go to the Tenders Board.
sections.tip: Framework agreements are rarely recommended for estimated expenditure below €184,000, because each need requires a mini-competition.

sections.lead: Framework contracts and agreements have no minimum duration but should not exceed four years, or five exceptionally, to respect non-exclusivity.
must: Orders or call-offs must be created before the end date and usually run no more than two to three months afterwards.
In projects, delivery must fall within the implementation period.
sections.tip: Framework contracts and agreements concluded through an international call are available to all Council of Europe entities; one-off contracts are not.

procurementStages.warning: Once the tender is published, the ordering method (ranking, pooling, rota or quotas) cannot be changed, so define it carefully in the tender documents.
procurementStages.best: Keep the number of suppliers in a multiple framework contract reasonable. Dividing the estimated budget by the number of consultants shows whether each supplier's expected turnover is credible.
checklist: Decide whether the need is one-off, recurring or variable
Choose simple or multiple framework contract
Choose ranking or pooling and state it in the tender
Set the maximum number of suppliers to select
For framework agreements, plan at least three suppliers per lot
Keep duration within four years (five exceptionally)
Check for overlap with existing framework contracts

procurementStages.name: Thresholds & Procedure
procurementStages.remember: Total foreseeable value decides the procedure — never split.
keyFacts: international public call and Tenders Board
procurementStages.example: A team estimates €170,000 for translations over four years, but the project may be extended. The value is close to €184,000 and could exceed it. The correct action is to launch an international public call for tenders from the start, because the Tenders Board cannot approve a launch retroactively.
procurementStages.title: Calculate the Threshold & Choose the Procedure
procurementStages.lead: Estimate the total value of the need to determine whether a direct award, a competitive bidding procedure or an international public call for tenders applies.
procurementStages.understand: The threshold is the estimated total value of the need, excluding VAT, over the full contract life, including renewals, lots and all orders or call-offs.
procurementStages.do: Calculate per need, not per supplier or year, and choose the procedure matching the value and funding source.
procurementStages.check: No need has been split artificially, and if the value may approach €184,000, an international public call for tenders is chosen.

sections.lead: The threshold is set by the total estimated value before VAT over the full life of the contract, not per year.
items: Include all renewals, tranches and options (works).
Add the value of every lot.
Include every possible order or call-off.
Calculate the value regardless of the number of suppliers.
Use the total value of the service contract.

sections.lead: A direct award is a contract without competition, allowed only below small amounts or in exceptional cases.
items: Up to €2,000 (goods, general services, works) or €6,000 (intellectual services), on a memorandum to the CCM justified by the supplier's expertise (Rule No. 1395, Article 22.4).
Urgency not attributable to the buyer (Financial Regulations Article 40.3.c, Rule Article 22.1.a).
Only one supplier can meet the technical need.
Facts or legal rights make competition impossible.
must: The CCM decides on exceptional direct awards below €184,000, and the Tenders Board decides from €184,000.
Extrabudgetary-funded direct awards from €55,000 to €184,000 must first receive a DLAPIL Legal Compliance Review.

sections.lead: Competitive bidding applies between €2,000 (or €6,000) and €184,000, under the sole responsibility of the CCM.
must: The buyer entity must invite at least three suppliers, or nine for a multiple framework contract with a pool of three.
Extrabudgetary-funded competitive bidding procedures from €55,000 to €184,000 must receive a Legal Compliance Review.
If all offers exceed €184,000, the buyer entity must cancel the procedure and launch an international call.

sections.lead: An international call applies when the total value is estimated to exceed €184,000, or if there is even a slight risk of reaching it.
must: The Tenders Board must authorise the launch, on request from the CCM with a summary memo to the Tenders Board Secretary.
An international call must allow at least three weeks for submission.
The Tenders Board cannot approve a launch retroactively.

sections.lead: Two further procedures exist for hard-to-define needs and small purchases.
items: For needs where the technical solution is hard to define, or a proof of concept. It uses a descriptive document, a published notice and rounds of discussion that may eliminate bidders; the Tenders Board validates the results.
Under Article 21.2 of Rule No. 1395, a competitive bidding purchase below €10,000 excluding VAT may compare the public prices of three or more suppliers instead of inviting tenders.
must: Screenshots of the compared public prices must be archived.

sections.lead: Goods or services for project beneficiaries are bought only through one-off contracts, by competitive bidding or international call depending on value.
items: DLAPIL tailor-made version, available on request.
Signed by the Council, the supplier and the beneficiary.
Ownership transfers to the beneficiary when it is signed.
sections.tip: Consult DIT on IT requirements.

sections.lead: Three practices can push a purchase into the wrong procedure.
items: Dividing purchases without objective reason to stay below thresholds; it is prohibited and a red flag for fraud.
If a later procedure covers needs that could have been included earlier, the threshold is calculated on the combined amount.
Amendments may push the total above the original threshold.

procurementStages.warning: Never split requirements or shorten contract terms to stay below a threshold. Artificial splitting is prohibited and treated as a red flag for fraud.
procurementStages.best: If the estimate is close to €184,000 or may grow through extensions, amendments or other directorates using the contract, launch an international public call for tenders from the outset.
checklist: Add up all lots, renewals, orders and call-offs before VAT
Calculate per need over the whole period of reference
Apply €2,000 / €6,000 for direct award
Use competitive bidding from €2,000 / €6,000 up to €184,000
Use an international public call above €184,000
Plan the Legal Compliance Review for extrabudgetary funds from €55,000 to €184,000
Use the procedure selection tool on the Procurement page

procurementStages.name: Tender Design
procurementStages.remember: Publish the criteria once; never change them afterwards.
keyFacts: minimum weight for price, in principle
bid as a share of turnover
procurementStages.example: A tender for a 1,000-person conference asks for prior experience organising events. That criterion is too vague to assess. The correct action is to require proven experience of events of comparable size, with a list of references as the supporting document.
procurementStages.title: Tender File, Lots & Assessment Criteria
procurementStages.lead: Build the tender package and set the exclusion, eligibility and award criteria that will decide the outcome.
procurementStages.understand: The tender file and act of engagement are mandatory for competitive procedures, and the criteria cannot be changed once the call is published.
procurementStages.do: Download fresh DLAPIL templates and set clear, proportionate eligibility criteria and weighted award criteria.
procurementStages.check: Criteria are objective, measurable and non-discriminatory, eligibility and award criteria do not overlap, and all weightings are published.

sections.lead: The tender package contains at least the tender file and the act of engagement, built from a fresh DLAPIL template.
items: The terms of reference and the tender rules.
A ready-to-sign contract containing bidders' statutory declarations.
must: Buyer entities must always download a new DLAPIL template, chosen by procedure, contract type, lots and language.
Documents published in two languages must state which version prevails, and machine translations must carry the standard disclaimer.
sections.tip: DGA and EDQM have their own templates.

sections.lead: Lots split a tender into separate competitions in the same call, increasing competition and letting specialised suppliers bid.
must: Lots may only be used if each lot can be awarded to a different supplier.
The procedure is determined by the total value of all lots.
sections.tip: Avoid overlapping lots, and do not use lots when a single supplier is needed.

sections.lead: The exclusion criteria in Appendix I to Rule No. 1395 apply to every purchase and cannot be deleted or changed, only supplemented.
items: Final judgment for participation in a criminal organisation, corruption, fraud, money laundering, terrorist financing or offences, child labour or trafficking in human beings.
Bankruptcy, liquidation, insolvency or a similar procedure.
A final judgment for an offence affecting professional integrity or serious misconduct.
Failure to pay social security contributions, taxes and dues.
An entity created to circumvent tax, social or other legal obligations.
Involvement in mismanagement of Council of Europe or public funds.
Being, or appearing to be, in a conflict of interest.
Retired staff and staff who left under an early departure scheme.
People employed by the Council now or on the launch date.
Failure to fulfil a Council contract in the previous three years leading to refused payment or termination.
UN Security Council or EU restrictive measures, including those on a legal person's owners or executives.
sections.tip: The signed declaration of agreement in DLAPIL acts of engagement serves as the declaration; e-procurement users confirm it online.

sections.lead: Eligibility criteria set the minimum financial, economic, technical or professional capacity needed to perform the contract.
must: Each eligibility criterion must be clear, objective, verifiable, proportionate and answerable with yes or no, with a defined supporting document.
items: Do not use words such as sufficient or relevant.
Do not require experience limited to Council of Europe projects.
Do not set overly prescriptive requirements.
sections.tip: As a guide, the bid should represent between 15% and 35% of the bidder's turnover.

sections.lead: Award criteria score quality and price to find the best value for money, and must not repeat eligibility criteria.
items: How the bidder will do the work.
How well the bidder grasps the objective.
The skills of the people proposed.
In principle at least 20 points, and weighted higher the more standard the service.
must: Weightings, including sub-criteria, must be published and cannot be changed.

sections.lead: A minimum score can limit who is invited to negotiations or included in a framework contract pool.
must: Any minimum score must be stated in the tender file.
Without a minimum score, all eligible suppliers up to the announced maximum number must be admitted to the pool.

procurementStages.warning: Assessment criteria and their weightings cannot be modified or subdivided once the call for tenders is published.
procurementStages.best: Keep eligibility requirements proportionate. Lower experience or turnover requirements attract new and innovative suppliers, and you can cap financial dependence instead of demanding a high turnover.
checklist: Download new tender file and act of engagement templates from DLAPIL
Decide on lots and avoid overlaps
Keep all exclusion criteria from Appendix I
Add the restrictive measures criterion
Define yes/no eligibility criteria with supporting documents
Weight award criteria, with price at least 20 points
State any minimum score in the tender file

procurementStages.name: Terms & Specifications
procurementStages.remember: Describe the objective, not the means; keep the three non-negotiable clauses.
keyFacts: usual notice period for tacit renewal (minimum 1 month)
procurementStages.example: A hotel will only sign its own contract terms, which give jurisdiction to national courts. The correct action is to accept the hotel's terms only if they are balanced and include the Council's clauses on disclosure, use of the name and logo, and disputes. If the hotel refuses, the CCM decides and records the decision.
procurementStages.title: Tender Rules, Prices & Contract Terms
procurementStages.lead: Set the rules for submission, the financial offer format, duration, renewal and legal conditions, and write specifications based on objectives.
procurementStages.understand: Tender rules, prices, duration, renewal and conditions fixed in the tender define the future contract and limit later changes.
procurementStages.do: Complete each part of the act of engagement and tender file deliberately, consulting DLAPIL for non-standard legal conditions.
procurementStages.check: Deadlines, offer validity, the price format, renewal clause, specific conditions and the three non-negotiable clauses are all in place.

sections.lead: Decide who may bid and how offers are submitted, and keep offers valid for 180 calendar days from the deadline.
items: Decide whether individuals may bid or only legal persons and consortia.
Members are jointly and severally liable.
must: Late offers are inadmissible.
International calls must allow at least three weeks, with offers sent to cdm@coe.int unless e-procurement is used.
When e-procurement is used, offers received outside the platform are excluded.

sections: Act of engagement and financial offer

sections.lead: The act of engagement holds the supplier and bank details, financial offer, declaration of agreement, signature boxes and legal conditions.
must: A bidder that fails to complete or sign the act of engagement is normally excluded automatically.
A missing financial offer cannot be completed after opening.
items: Use deliverable-based units in framework contracts.
Use time-based units in framework contracts.
sections.tip: Add the clause allowing an hourly fee to be calculated as the daily fee divided by 8.

sections.lead: Give quantities or estimated volumes and a detailed price table so that offers can be compared.
must: Any price update or revision must be provided for in the tender, and a revision under such a clause is recorded in a document signed by both parties, not an amendment.
sections.tip: Link revisions to a relevant official index with a margin, and avoid exclusion levels (maximum prices) unless there is a strong objective reason such as a donor cap.

sections.lead: Decide before publication how long the contract lasts and whether it can be renewed.
items: The contract ends at its term.
Both parties sign a renewal before expiry.
The contract renews unless a party objects; best for framework contracts and agreements.
must: A one-off contract must have a delivery deadline.
A multi-year contract should last no more than four years, or five in specific circumstances.
The notice period to object to tacit renewal is usually three months and must never be less than one month.

sections.lead: The General Conditions, called legal conditions in DLAPIL templates, cover VAT, confidentiality, data protection, payment and disputes; three clauses are non-negotiable.
items: The Council may disclose the terms for audit, governance and transparency.
Use of the Council's name and logo
The supplier may not use them without permission.
must: A supplier's own terms, for example a hotel's, may be accepted only if they are balanced and include the three non-negotiable clauses.
sections.tip: Internet purchase terms can be accepted exceptionally under the CCM's documented responsibility.

sections.lead: Technical or large-scale purchases use supplementary general conditions plus specific contractual conditions.
items: Supplementary general conditions for consultancy and similar work.
Supplementary general conditions for goods and services.
Supplementary general conditions for building works.
Supplementary general conditions for IT purchases.
sections.tip: Add specific conditions such as indices, warranty, penalties or building access with the Procurement Unit's help, and set penalties high enough to be useful but not so high that they discourage bids.

sections.lead: Specify the objective to be achieved, not the means.
items: Avoid them or add or equivalent.
Do not mix administrative and technical content.
Give enough information so that previous suppliers have no advantage.
Take account of total cost of ownership, warranty and maintenance.
Define them to support performance monitoring and penalties.

procurementStages.warning: Never accept contract terms without the three non-negotiable clauses (disclosure, name and logo, disputes) unless the CCM takes the documented decision described in the guide.
procurementStages.best: For framework contracts and agreements, choose tacit renewal. It is far easier to manage than renewal by written agreement, especially with many suppliers.
checklist: Define eligible tenderer types and subcontracting rules
Set the submission deadline (at least three weeks for international calls)
Confirm 180-day offer validity or consult DLAPIL
Provide a detailed price or fee table with volumes
Decide on any price revision clause and index
Choose duration and renewal option
Check the three non-negotiable clauses are included
Write objective-based technical specifications

procurementStages.name: Authorise & Launch
procurementStages.remember: No approval, no launch; same answers to everyone.
procurementStages.example: An EU-funded €90,000 competitive bidding procedure is ready to launch. Because it is extrabudgetary and between €55,000 and €184,000, a Legal Compliance Review is required first. The correct action is to send a Request for LCR to DLAPIL and submit the documents to the CCM only after DLAPIL's visa.
procurementStages.title: Authorise, Publish & Manage Questions
procurementStages.lead: Obtain the required approval, invite or publish the call, and handle questions and deadline extensions fairly.
procurementStages.understand: The approval route depends on the procedure, the value and the funding source: the CCM, the CCM after a DLAPIL Legal Compliance Review, or the Tenders Board.
procurementStages.do: Submit tender documents for approval through the correct route, then invite at least three suppliers or publish, preferably via e-procurement.
procurementStages.check: Written approval is on file before launch, and all bidders receive the same answers at the same time.

sections.lead: The approval route depends on the procedure and the value.
items: A memorandum validated by the CCM.
A memorandum stating specification, cost, justification and supplier, to the CCM below €184,000 or the Tenders Board from €184,000.
The CCM approves the documents in writing.
The CCM sends the documents and an explanatory note to the Tenders Board.

sections.lead: Since 1 February 2025, extrabudgetary-funded competitive bidding and exceptional direct awards between €55,000 and €184,000 need a DLAPIL Legal Compliance Review before CCM approval.
items: Send the request through the DLAPIL request form with the title Request for LCR.
Attach the direct award memorandum or all tender documents.
State the procedure, the estimated total expenditure, the funding source and the entities already consulted.
DLAPIL processes complete requests within 5 working days and gives its visa in writing.
With the DLAPIL visa, the documents go to the CCM, who approves the launch.
sections.tip: Call-offs under framework agreements are exempt, because they are not a procurement procedure.

sections.lead: The Tenders Board authorises the launch of international calls and validates their results, and is consulted on negotiations, amendments and direct awards.
items: The CCM e-mails the documents and an explanatory memo to the Tenders Board Secretariat.
The Secretariat gives members at least 48 hours (two working days) on the Tenders Board SharePoint.
The buyer entity answers members' questions on the SharePoint.
The decision is posted on the SharePoint and sent by e-mail or e-procurement.
The buyer entity makes any requested changes and the Secretariat validates the final version.

sections.lead: Competitive bidding invites suppliers by e-mail, while international calls are published by the Tenders Board Secretariat.
must: In competitive bidding, the buyer entity must e-mail the tender documents to at least three suppliers and record the reasons if this is impossible.
For international calls, the Tenders Board Secretariat publishes on the CoE website, and the Board may add the OJEU, e-procurement, media or permanent representations.
items: E-procurement mandatory for all tenders above €2,000 or €6,000.

sections.lead: All bidders receive the same answers through a single, anonymised Q&A document.
must: The tender must state the e-mail address and deadline for questions, using a non-nominative address separate from the one receiving offers.
The buyer entity must distribute the anonymised Q&A document through every channel used to publish or invite.
No answer may be given later than 48 hours before the submission deadline.
Questions received by other channels are not answered, and there is no other contact with bidders during the tender.

sections.lead: The submission deadline may be extended only in exceptional circumstances.
must: An extension must be decided before the deadline expires and approved by the CCM.
sections.tip: Consult DLAPIL or the Procurement Unit beforehand.

procurementStages.warning: Do not answer bidders' questions outside the published Q&A procedure. Every bidder must have access to the same information at the same time.
procurementStages.best: Publish at the right time: avoid launching during the summer break or setting a Monday-morning deadline, and use the e-procurement link to spread the call on relevant networks.
checklist: Identify the approval route by value and funding
Request the Legal Compliance Review if it is required
Obtain written approval from the CCM or Tenders Board
Invite at least three suppliers or publish
Set the questions e-mail address and deadline
Publish anonymised Q&A to all bidders
Extend the deadline only before expiry, with CCM approval

procurementStages.name: Open & Evaluate
procurementStages.remember: Admissible, not excluded, eligible — only then score.
procurementStages.example: One bidder sent a missing CV late and also left the financial offer blank. The missing CV is minor information and can be clarified. The correct action is to exclude the bid anyway, because a missing financial offer cannot be completed after opening.
procurementStages.title: Open, Analyse & Evaluate Bids
procurementStages.lead: Open offers securely after the deadline and assess them in sequence: admissibility, exclusion, eligibility and award criteria.
procurementStages.understand: Bids are assessed by at least two authorised staff members, strictly against the criteria published in the tender file.
procurementStages.do: Record the opening, check admissibility, apply exclusion and eligibility as pass or fail, then score award criteria with written justification.
procurementStages.check: Every score has an objective written justification, and any red flags or clarification requests are documented.

sections.lead: Offers are opened only after the deadline, and receipt and prices are recorded and confirmed by those opening.
items: Offers open automatically after the deadline and one authorised staff member of the buyer entity opens them.
At least two authorised staff members of the buyer entity open the offers.
International call by e-mail (Tenders Board Secretariat)
The Secretariat opens offers sent to cdm@coe.int with an authorised member of the buyer entity and shares the record.

sections.lead: Check admissibility first, analysing each lot separately.
items: Inadmissible unless the delay was caused by the Council, for example a system failure.
Inadmissible, although missing minor information may be requested.
Bids above a published exclusion level are excluded.

sections.lead: Admissible bids are then checked against the exclusion and eligibility criteria, which are pass or fail.
must: The buyer entity must exclude any bid that fails an exclusion criterion or whose act of engagement is not signed.
With EU funds, the buyer entity must check the EU sanctions list using the WebFOCUS report.
A bid that fails an eligibility criterion is ineligible, and exceeding another criterion does not compensate unless the tender file says so.
sections.tip: Where risk requires, ask the selected supplier for criminal record and tax certificates before signing.

sections.lead: Only eligible bids are scored, using the published weightings.
items: Score each one out of 10 with a clear written assessment.
Multiply each score by its published weight.
Calculate financial scores against the cheapest offer; if price is the only criterion, the cheapest offer wins.
sections.tip: Use the DLAPIL and Procurement Unit assessment templates or e-procurement; for Ordinary Budget purchases where all offers exceed the budget, scoring against the budget is good practice.

sections.lead: Under Article 17.2 of Rule No. 1395, offers may be clarified only with non-essential information that does not change their main features or distort competition.
must: Clarification requests must be made in writing, kept on record and reported to the CCM or Tenders Board with the results.
A clarification that would significantly change a bid requires a negotiation round.

sections.lead: Some bidders and offers need special treatment.
items: Bids from current staff, or from people employed on the launch date, are excluded.
Retired staff and those who left under an early departure measure cannot receive new contracts.
Need their employer's approval and leave and must have no conflict.
Red flags that may be excluded with an explanatory memo.
The same bidder may not submit more than one bid.
May be clarified rather than automatically excluded.

sections.lead: Assessors look for signs of fraud, corruption, collusion or bid rigging.
must: An assessor who sees any indication of fraud must report it immediately to their manager, copying the Director of the DIO.
sections.tip: If the DIO opens an investigation, ask DLAPIL whether to reject the bids without waiting for the outcome.

procurementStages.warning: A missing or incomplete financial offer, or an unsigned act of engagement, cannot be corrected after opening, and the bid must normally be excluded.
procurementStages.best: Write a detailed justification for every technical score. Clear analysis makes approval easier and lets you answer later enquiries without disclosing other bidders' information.
checklist: Open offers only after the deadline and record receipt
Use at least two authorised assessors
Check admissibility and that the act of engagement is signed
Apply exclusion and eligibility criteria as pass or fail
Score award criteria out of 10 with written justification
Check EU sanctions list when EU funds are used
Document all clarification requests in writing

procurementStages.name: Negotiate & Award
procurementStages.remember: Sign with the winner first, then notify the others within 15 days.
keyFacts: to complain to the Tenders Board
procurementStages.example: An international call produced offers that are all well above budget. The correct action is a memo to the Tenders Board asking either to negotiate with the eligible bidders, to relaunch, or to cancel. The memo must explain why the call failed and justify the chosen option.
procurementStages.title: Negotiate, Award & Notify
procurementStages.lead: Negotiate where it adds value, obtain the award decision, inform bidders and deal with unsuccessful procedures and complaints.
procurementStages.understand: The CCM decides awards for competitive bidding procedures and the Tenders Board decides for international calls, based on the buyer entity's reasoned recommendation.
procurementStages.do: Seek authorisation before negotiating, submit the analysis and recommendation, then notify successful and unsuccessful bidders in writing.
procurementStages.check: Unsuccessful bidders are notified within 15 days of the successful notification, with the enquiry procedure explained.

sections.lead: Negotiation is possible in all tendering procedures (Rule No. 1395, Articles 20 and 21.8) to improve the offer, agree legal changes or settle final details.
must: A negotiation must not significantly change the specifications.
The buyer entity must send a memo explaining why, with whom and on what to the CCM (competitive bidding) or the Tenders Board (international call).
The buyer entity must invite all eligible bidders unless exclusion is justified, document everything and get changes confirmed in writing.
sections.tip: Involve DLAPIL for legal clauses and DIT or DGS for technical items.

sections.lead: The CCM decides the award in competitive bidding, and the Tenders Board in international calls.
items: Submit a reasoned recommendation to the CCM, who decides.
The CCM validates the memo, assessment tables and recommendation and sends them to the Tenders Board Secretary; the Board scrutinises the analysis and decides.
must: The buyer entity must never select more suppliers than the announced maximum.
sections.tip: Auditors expect the CCM to justify repeated use of the same suppliers over a year, supported by a WebFOCUS report.

sections.lead: Sign with the winner first, then tell the others.
items: Complete signature before telling the others.
Within 15 days, in writing, with the reason and the Article 24 enquiry procedure.
must: Only the winner's amount, name and country may be disclosed to unsuccessful bidders.
sections.tip: Results of international calls are published, and e-procurement sends notification letters automatically.

sections.lead: A call is unfruitful if no or too few bids arrive, none meet the criteria, or prices greatly exceed the budget.
items: Ask to negotiate with a supplier (Articles 18.3 and 21.10).
must: The CCM (competitive bidding) or the Tenders Board (international call) must decide on a justifying memo, and bidders must be informed in writing.

sections.lead: A procedure may be discontinued at any time before the award, without giving reasons or paying compensation (Article 18.2).
must: The CCM decides for competitive bidding and the Tenders Board for international calls, and the buyer entity must inform tenderers in writing.

sections.lead: Unsuccessful bidders have up to three steps of recourse, none of which suspends the award or the start of the contract.
items: Within 7 days of notification; the buyer entity replies without undue delay.
Within 30 days; the Board replies within 30 days, and for competitive bidding this decision is final.
Appeal to an ad hoc review board
International calls only, within 30 days, with a reply within 60 days.

procurementStages.warning: Sign the contract with the selected supplier before notifying unsuccessful bidders, and never disclose details of other bids beyond the winner's amount, name and country.
procurementStages.best: When only one offer is received, you may still negotiate, but do not tell the bidder that no other bids were received.
checklist: Request CCM or Tenders Board authorisation before negotiating
Record negotiations and obtain written bid confirmations
Submit the reasoned award recommendation
Respect the maximum number of suppliers announced
Sign the contract, then notify unsuccessful bidders within 15 days
Reply to enquiries using only the assessment records

procurementStages.name: Contract Signing
procurementStages.remember: PO first, signature second, work third.
keyFacts: create a new supplier in FIMS
procurementStages.example: A consultant offers to start work on Monday, but the contract has not yet been countersigned. The correct action is to raise the PO in FIMS, have the CCM countersign, and send the signed PDF before any work starts.
procurementStages.title: Contract Review & Signature
procurementStages.lead: Complete the final checks and administrative steps so the contract is properly committed in FIMS and countersigned before any work starts.
procurementStages.understand: A budgetary commitment (PO) is mandatory before the Organisation signs any contract, and no goods or services may be provided before signature.
procurementStages.do: Check the documents, register new suppliers via MSA 4002, raise the PO, countersign and send the signed copy to the supplier.
procurementStages.check: The act of engagement is complete, signed by the supplier, unaltered, matches any negotiations, and the PO exists before countersignature.

sections.lead: Check the contract documents carefully before signature.
items: They are correct, reflect any negotiated outcome and have not been modified by the supplier.
It is complete and signed by the supplier.
The supplier's name and the bank account holder are the same.

sections.lead: Set up the supplier and the commitment in FIMS before signing.
items: Create the supplier (buyer entity, then TPA)
For a new supplier, the buyer entity submits MSA 4002 and TPA processes it.
The CCM countersigns only after the commitment exists.
must: The commitment in FIMS must be made before the internal signature process.

sections.lead: Who signs depends on whether the contract is a financial as well as a legal commitment.
items: A legal and financial commitment, signed by the CCM unless signature is expressly delegated.
Only a legal commitment unless it includes a minimum purchase, so a duly authorised person may sign it, although CCM signature is advisable.
must: Each selected supplier must sign the contract.
The buyer entity must enter the applicable VAT requirements in the invoicing table, as instructed by Protocol.

sections.lead: Countersign with a wet-ink or electronic signature, then send and archive.
items: A scanned act of engagement signed by the supplier can be countersigned electronically by the CCM.
E-mail a signed PDF copy to the contact named in the contract, or post a paper copy if requested.

sections.lead: The contract is made up of several documents.
must: If supplier documents contain internet links, the buyer entity must download those pages on the date of signature and add them to the file.

sections.lead: Once signed, a framework contract or agreement can be shared so colleagues with similar needs can use it.
sections.tip: Add it to the Organisation's database with help from the Procurement Unit.

procurementStages.warning: Never let a supplier start work, or sign any contract, before a PO has been raised in FIMS and the Organisation has signed.
procurementStages.best: Save copies of any web pages referred to in the contract on the date of signature, in case the supplier later changes its conditions.
checklist: Verify documents are unaltered and reflect negotiations
Confirm the act of engagement is complete and signed
Create the new supplier via MSA 4002
Raise the PO in FIMS before signature
Fill in VAT requirements in the invoicing table
Countersign and send a PDF copy to the supplier
Add framework contracts to the shared database

procurementStages.name: Contract Management
procurementStages.remember: Amend before expiry; never change scope; watch the ceiling.
keyFacts: ceiling for competitive bidding framework contracts
call-off increase the CCM may authorise
procurementStages.example: A framework contract awarded through competitive bidding has reached €150,000 in orders, with more training sessions planned. The correct action is to contact DLAPIL immediately and prepare an international public call for tenders, approved by the Tenders Board, before spending exceeds €184,000.
procurementStages.title: Deadlines, Amendments, Orders & Renewal
procurementStages.lead: Manage the contract actively: track deadlines, amend correctly, accept deliverables, order within thresholds and renew or end the contract on time.
procurementStages.understand: The buyer entity monitors execution, and amendments may change how the contract is managed but never its main purpose, scope, volume or nature.
procurementStages.do: Track deadlines, sign orders and call-offs through the CCM, monitor cumulative spending and document every change in writing.
procurementStages.check: Cumulative spending stays below the threshold of the original procedure, and every extension or amendment is agreed before expiry.

sections.lead: The delivery deadline differs from the contract end date, which also covers acceptance, payment and warranty.
must: A deadline extension must be legitimate, must not jeopardise the project, must be agreed before the original deadline expires, and counts as an amendment.
When a deadline is missed, the CCM decides whether to apply penalties, reduce payment, terminate or set a new deadline.
sections.tip: Set realistic deadlines, use reminders and contact the provider before the deadline.

sections.lead: A contract can be amended only while it is in force, with both parties' agreement, and without distorting the original competition.
sections.tip: Typical amendments change deadlines, contact details, supplier name or bank details.
items: Obtain the CCM's written agreement before proposing the amendment.
By e-mail with the standard wording and the CCM in copy, or by a document, stating which provisions are supplemented or replaced.
The supplier agrees by return e-mail or signs the document.
must: Call-off amendments up to 10% of the original value need CCM authorisation, and above 10% the buyer entity must consult DLAPIL.

sections.lead: Accept deliverables in writing after checking them against the contract specifications.
must: A refusal of deliverables must be sent to the supplier with reasons; a second refusal may be treated as a breach.
The acceptance certificate must be attached to the payment order validated by the CCM.
sections.tip: For events, keep photographs and signed attendance sheets.

sections.lead: Each order identifies the right supplier and fixes concrete deliverables, a deadline and a lump-sum price.
items: Apply the ranking or pooling rules in the contract.
State concrete deliverables, a deadline and a lump-sum price, but not the number of days.
The CCM signs after the PO has been raised.
must: Spending under a competitive bidding framework contract must not exceed €184,000; if it might, the buyer entity must contact DLAPIL immediately, and the remedy is an international call approved by the Tenders Board.

sections.lead: Each call-off is a mini-competition among the preselected suppliers, evaluated on the published award criteria.
must: The buyer entity must send each call-off with terms of reference and a deadline, without revealing the other suppliers' identities.
Call-offs above €184,000 must go to the Tenders Board, and the CCM signs each call-off.
items: A supplier that fails to justify non-participation more than three times may be removed.
After three call-offs with all tenders more than 20% above market price, the Council may tender outside the agreement.

sections.lead: Contracts end by mutual consent, by unilateral termination as a last resort, or continue by renewal.
items: Both parties agree in writing to end the contract.
Only for breach where no negotiated solution can be found, after consulting DLAPIL, with all exchanges in writing.
Completed before expiry, separately with each supplier, with the CCM's agreement.

procurementStages.warning: Exceeding €184,000 under a framework contract awarded through competitive bidding is a severe breach of the rules. If there is any risk of this, launch an international public call.
procurementStages.best: Use the Procurement Unit's Excel tracking tables to follow every order or call-off against the contract ceiling, and tell the Tenders Board Secretary early if an announced budget will be significantly exceeded.
checklist: Set reminders for every delivery deadline
Agree extensions and amendments in writing before expiry
Accept deliverables in writing against specifications
Issue orders with deliverables, a deadline and a lump-sum price
Have the CCM sign orders and call-offs after the PO
Track cumulative spend against the procedure threshold
Renew or retender before the contract expires

procurementStages.name: Contract Execution & Payment
procurementStages.remember: Right invoice, right account, VAT settled before signing.
procurementStages.example: A French supplier asks to be paid in 90 days in exchange for a lower price. French law prohibits payment terms longer than 60 days net. The correct action is to refuse 90 days and, if different terms are needed, agree them with TPA and write them into the contract.
procurementStages.title: Invoices, Payments & VAT
procurementStages.lead: Make sure invoices are correct, paid on time to the right account, and that VAT and delivery terms are settled before signature.
procurementStages.understand: Each directorate receives and validates invoices, TPA pays them by bank transfer in euros, and VAT must be clarified before signing.
procurementStages.do: Check each invoice against the contract and acceptance certificate, apply the agreed payment terms and follow Protocol's VAT exemption procedures.
procurementStages.check: The invoice meets all formal requirements, the payee account belongs to the supplier, and the VAT regime is correct.

sections.lead: An invoice must contain specific information before it can be paid.
items: The Council of Europe, with the department on the second line.
Name, address and VAT number if any.
The deliverables and the contract fees.
Sub-totals and total in the contract currency.
must: An invoice with an intra-EU VAT number must include the exemption wording referring to Articles 143 and 151 of Council Directive 2006/112/EC.

sections.lead: Unless agreed otherwise, the payment term is 60 days from receipt of the invoice or execution of the contract, whichever is later.
must: Payment must be made within the contract deadline to the bank account named in the contract, which must be held by the supplier.
For French suppliers, French law prohibits payment terms longer than 60 days net or 45 days end of month.

sections.lead: Staged payments must be set out in the tender file and contract.
must: Shorter terms in exchange for a discount must be approved by TPA and written into the contract.
sections.tip: Immediate payment is only for exceptional, justified cases, and TPA's minimum lead time is about 10 days.

sections.lead: Payments are normally by bank transfer in euros, with cards, cheques or cash only as exceptions.
items: Create the purchase order in FIMS.
must: A card payment must not exceed €5,000 per purchase, and card spending must not exceed €30,000 per month for the whole Organisation.
sections.tip: For internet purchases, consider the public prices procedure below €10,000; the supplier's terms may be accepted under the CCM's documented responsibility.

sections.lead: For goods, Incoterms define who organises and insures transport and from what point.
sections.tip: Use DAP (Delivered at Place) to a Council of Europe address so the supplier is responsible until delivery, and contact Protocol for details.

sections.lead: Goods and services for the Council's official use may be exempt from VAT, with separate procedures for goods and for services.
must: With a new supplier, the buyer entity must establish its VAT status and the exact nature of the purchase to determine the place of taxation.
sections.tip: Protocol is the point of contact for all VAT questions.

procurementStages.warning: Always clarify VAT before signing and sending the contract or order form, and never pay into an account not held by the supplier named in the contract.
procurementStages.best: When suppliers need cash flow, such as in works or IT, set out a payment schedule in the tender file. It encourages more candidates to bid.
checklist: Check invoice addressee, letterhead and mandatory details
Match invoice lines to contract fees and accepted deliverables
Confirm the bank account holder is the supplier
Apply 60-day terms unless others are agreed
Stay within €5,000 per card purchase
Settle the VAT regime with Protocol before signature
Use DAP Incoterms for goods deliveries

procurementStages.name: Performance & Filing
procurementStages.example: At the end of a printing contract, deliveries were repeatedly late. Poor performance alone does not stop the supplier from bidding again. The correct action is to record the evaluation and add clear delivery targets linked to penalties in the next tender.
procurementStages.title: Supplier Performance, Follow-up & Archiving
procurementStages.lead: Assess how suppliers perform, use the lessons for the next tender, and keep a complete, audit-ready file.
procurementStages.understand: Performance follow-up improves future tenders, and complete archives support audits; poor past performance alone does not exclude a supplier.
procurementStages.do: Assess suppliers during and at the end of the contract, and archive all procurement documents for 10 years.
procurementStages.check: The file holds the tender documents, all bids, assessments, negotiations, memos, contract and amendments.

sections.lead: Evaluate the supplier against the agreed deadlines, quality and service, during the contract and at the end.
items: Whether costs stay within the contract.
sections.tip: Use a questionnaire scored, for example, from 1 (very poor) to 10 (very good); the Procurement Unit has templates and can help set it up before the tender.

sections.lead: Poor past performance does not in itself prevent a supplier from bidding again.
sections.tip: The optional exclusion criterion covers suppliers who failed contractual obligations in the past three years, leading to refused payment or termination; build lessons such as clear targets linked to penalties into the next tender.

sections.lead: The DGA Procurement Unit monitors performance through KPIs and maps purchases using e-procurement and FIMS data.
sections.tip: Extract data for your CCM or directorate through WebFOCUS reports; procurement categories help define strategies for intellectual services, works and IT.

sections.lead: Keep all contract documents for 10 years.
items: The published or sent tender package.
The signed contract and any changes.
sections.tip: Each directorate keeps its files, usually in DMS; the buyer entity keeps execution documents such as acceptance separately, and TPA keeps invoices and payment requests.

sections.lead: The e-procurement platform, developed by DIT and supported by the Procurement Unit, centralises the tender process and keeps a full audit trail.
items: Calls are published on the platform.
Questions and answers are handled centrally.
Scoring is done on the platform.
sections.tip: Training on Procurement optimisation and e-procurement gives Super-User status; see also the intranet Procurement page, the DLAPIL and Tenders Board pages and the free internet suppliers portal.

sections.lead: Social networks can be used to promote calls and source suppliers.
must: While a call is in progress, staff involved should not be openly connected with likely bidders or share or like their posts.

procurementStages.warning: Missing documents in the file, such as justifications for direct awards, assessments or proof of notification, are a recurring audit finding. Archive everything for 10 years.
procurementStages.best: Carry out an end-of-contract assessment before retendering, and draft the new tender documents to fix the weaknesses it identifies.
checklist: Assess supplier performance during the contract
Complete an end-of-contract evaluation
Record lessons learned for the next tender
Archive tender documents, bids and assessments
File negotiation records, memos, contract and amendments
Keep execution and acceptance documents separately
Retain the procurement file for 10 years

grantStages.name: Foundations
grantStages.title: What a grant is and when Rule 1374 applies
grantStages.lead: A grant finances a project, a specified action or a grantee's operations to advance the Organisation's values. Rule 1374 implements Article 43 bis of the Financial Regulations for every grant procedure.
grantStages.remember: Two purposes, both required: help the grantee, advance the Organisation.
keyFacts: Financial Regulations basis, implemented by Rule 1374
normal maximum for an operational grant agreement
grantStages.example: A programme wants to fund a human rights NGO's annual running costs. The NGO's goals and the Council's values are both served, so a grant fits, but as an operational grant. Correct action: plan an operational grant agreement of no more than twelve consecutive months.
grantStages.understand: A grant must both help the grantee attain its own objectives and advance the Organisation's values or policies; the two conditions are cumulative.
grantStages.do: Confirm that both purposes are met and decide whether you are financing a project-related grant or an operational grant.
grantStages.check: Every staff member involved in the award process has completed the staff member declaration of interest.

sections.lead: A grant serves two cumulative purposes; if either is missing, a grant is not the right instrument.
items: It assists the grantee in attaining its own goals or objectives.
It fulfils a more general objective of advancing the Organisation's values or policies.
must: Every grant must meet both purposes at the same time.

sections.lead: Grants are foreseen by Article 43 bis of the Financial Regulations and implemented by Rule 1374.
items: Grants financed from the Organisation's own budget.
Grants financed from voluntary contributions by member states or others.
Grants financed under Grant Agreements with external donors.
must: Rule 1374 applies to every grant procedure, whatever the source of funding.

sections.lead: A grant finances either a project or a grantee's running costs, whatever the grantee's status, public or private, legal or natural person.
items: Finances a project or a specified action.
Finances a given grantee's operational expenditure.
must: An operational grant should not normally give rise to a grant agreement of more than twelve consecutive months.

sections.lead: Co-financing is the characteristic feature that distinguishes a grant from a service contract.
items: The grantee co-finances the action from its own or third-party resources.
No service contract may give rise to co-financing by the service supplier.
sections.tip: If the Council would pay the full cost of a service it needs, use the procurement rules instead.

sections.lead: Staff involved in a grant award process declare their interests before taking part.
must: Every staff member involved in a procurement or grant award process must complete the staff member declaration of interest.
sections.tip: Complete the declaration before taking part in any step of the procedure.

sections.lead: The guide follows the numbering of Rule 1374, and each template carries the number of the article it implements.
sections.tip: Template G14.1, for example, implements Article 14.1.

grantStages.warning: Both purposes of a grant are mandatory and cumulative; a financing that only serves the grantee, or only the Organisation, is not a grant.
grantStages.best: Record at the outset why the action meets both purposes; this justification will also anchor the objectives of the call.
checklist: Confirm the grantee's goals and the Organisation's objective are both served
Identify the funding source (Ordinary Budget, VC or donor agreement)
Classify the grant as project-related or operational
Keep operational grants to twelve consecutive months or less
Check that co-financing makes this a grant, not a service contract
Complete the staff member declaration of interest

grantStages.name: Principles
grantStages.title: The six general principles of Rule 1374
grantStages.lead: Article 2 sets six principles that apply to every grant: transparency, non-retroactivity, co-financing, non-cumulative awards, no profit and non-discrimination.
grantStages.remember: Count the whole procedure budget; never let the Council pay everything.
keyFacts: total procedure budget triggering a call
grantStages.example: A department plans five grants of €10,000 to local youth NGOs and suggests five direct awards. The reference figure is the €50,000 total, which passes the threshold. Correct action: launch a call for proposals and require each grantee to co-finance.
grantStages.understand: The principles govern every decision in the procedure, and breaching one can invalidate an award or make costs ineligible.
grantStages.do: Test the planned grant against each of the six principles before designing the call.
grantStages.check: The €15,000 threshold has been measured against the total estimated budget of the procedure, not the amount per grantee.
sections: The six principles at a glance

sections.lead: Article 2 sets six general principles that apply to every grant procedure.
items: Procedures of €15,000 or more require a published call for proposals.
The action must not already be completed when the agreement is signed.
The Council never finances the entire cost.
One Council grant per project, action or operational grantee.
Total funding cannot exceed the agreed budgeted expenses.
Applicants are treated equally unless a difference is objectively justified.

sections.lead: All grant award procedures of €15,000 or more require, in principle, a published call for proposals.
items: The threshold refers to the total estimated budget of the procedure, not the amount per grantee.
Five grants of €10,000 make €50,000, so the threshold is passed and a call is required.
must: Above the threshold, any exception to publication must be interpreted strictly.

sections.lead: Only three situations may justify not publishing a call once the €15,000 threshold is met.
items: An emergency beyond the awarding entity's control, of such magnitude that a call cannot be carried out.
The grantee's nature makes a call impossible, for example an international organisation acting alone in a given field.
The action is described in terms leaving no scope for a call, for instance partners approved by a donor and contractually predetermined.

sections.lead: The action financed must not already be completed when the agreement is signed.
items: Allowed but not recommended, provided eligible costs were incurred only after the closing date for proposals.
must: Eligible costs must not be incurred before the closing date for submission of proposals.
The grant agreement must state precisely the beginning and end of the implementation period.

sections.lead: The Council must not finance the entire cost of the action, the project or the grantee's operations.
items: Financial resources of the grantee or of other funders.
Staff time contributed by the grantee.
Moveable or immoveable, tangible or intangible assets.
Income generated by the action or project itself.
must: The grantee must contribute to financing the action from resources other than the Council grant.

sections.lead: Each action receives only one Council grant, and its total funding cannot exceed the agreed budget.
items: The Council awards only one grant to a given project, action or operational grantee.
A grant may not finance part of an action already financed by other means.
Several funders may each finance different parts of the action.
Total funding above the agreed budgeted expenses would be overfunding and breach the no-profit principle.

sections.lead: A difference in treatment of applicants in comparable situations is discriminatory unless it has an objective and reasonable justification.
items: Gender, disability, age, colour, language, religion, belief, marital or parental status, opinions, national, social or ethnic origin, national minority, wealth, birth, citizenship, sexual orientation or any other situation.
The principle applies to legal persons and their representatives, for example regarding place of establishment.
The difference must pursue a legitimate aim with proportionate means.
sections.tip: Restricting a call to applicants in one town is justified when the call aims to build civil society capacity in that town.

grantStages.warning: The €15,000 threshold applies to the total estimated budget of the procedure; splitting it into smaller grants does not avoid a call for proposals.
grantStages.best: Plan the agreement so that implementation begins after signature; it is the cleanest way to respect non-retroactivity.
checklist: Calculate the total estimated budget of the whole procedure
Publish a call if the total is €15,000 or more
Document any strict exception to publication
Ensure no eligible costs precede the submission deadline
Require the grantee to co-finance the action
