Check the action receives no other Council grant
Justify objectively any restriction on who may apply

grantStages.name: Procedure
grantStages.title: Choosing the route: direct award or call for proposals
grantStages.lead: The total estimated budget decides the route: below €15,000 a grant may be awarded directly; from €15,000 a competitive call for proposals is the rule.
grantStages.remember: Below €15,000 you may award directly; from €15,000, call.
grantStages.example: A project needs a single €12,000 grant to a regional ombudsman network. The total procedure budget is below €15,000. Correct action: the Commitments Officer adopts a G9.2A decision, which also appoints the Co-ordinator, and signs the agreement.
grantStages.understand: Direct award below €15,000 (Art. 2.1.2) needs only Template G9.2A; €15,000 or more requires a competitive call unless exceptional circumstances apply (Art. 2.1.3).
grantStages.do: Calculate the total procedure budget, select the route and open the matching decision template.
grantStages.check: Any direct award of €15,000 or more carries a duly justified Commitments Officer decision attached to the commitment request.

sections.lead: Under Article 2.1.2, a procedure with a total budget below €15,000 may be awarded without a call for proposals.
items: The Commitments Officer adopts the direct award decision; it also appoints the Co-ordinator.
The grant agreement is signed with the grantee.

sections.lead: From €15,000 the principle is a competitive call for proposals, run in eight steps.
items: Draft, approve and publish the call (G8.1A or G8.1B, with G8.2).
Publish the questions and answers to all potential applicants.
Template G13.1, with declarations of absence of conflicts of interest (G13.4).
Eligibility report, individual scores and consensus report (G14.1, G14.3, G14.4).
The Commitments Officer adopts the award decision (G14.6).
Send the letters to applicants (G14.8, G14.9A, G14.9B).

sections.lead: Under Article 2.1.3, a grant of €15,000 or more cannot be awarded without a call unless exceptional circumstances occur.
items: The Commitments Officer adopts a duly justified decision, which also appoints the Co-ordinator.
The grant agreement is signed with the grantee.
must: The Commitments Officer must justify the decision with reference to Article 2.1.3.
The justified decision must be attached to the request for commitment of funds (engagement de dépenses).

sections.lead: Only the competent Commitments Officer, or a representative by written delegation, can decide on a direct award.
sections.tip: The procedural guarantees for direct award are set out in Article 9 of the Rule.

grantStages.warning: A direct award of €15,000 or more is an exception that must be strictly justified under Article 2.1.3; an unreasoned G9.2B decision does not meet the Rule.
grantStages.best: Use the G3.1TAB follow-up table from the start of a competitive procedure to track each step and template.
checklist: Establish the total estimated budget of the procedure
Below €15,000: complete Template G9.2A and sign the agreement
From €15,000: launch the competitive procedure
For exceptional direct award, justify under Article 2.1.3 with G9.2B
Attach the justified decision to the commitment request
Track the steps in the Co-ordinator's follow-up table
templates: Decision on direct award equal to or exceeding €15,000

grantStages.name: Roles
grantStages.title: Who is responsible: Commitments Officer, Co-ordinator, Evaluation Committee
grantStages.lead: The Commitments Officer is responsible for the whole grant award procedure, appoints a Co-ordinator and an Evaluation Committee, and may delegate in writing.
grantStages.remember: The Commitments Officer decides; the Co-ordinator runs; the Committee evaluates.
grantStages.example: A Head of Department wants a cost centre manager to run a grant procedure on his behalf. Delegation is possible within his administrative entity. Correct action: delegate in writing under Article 31 of the Financial Regulations, then appoint the Co-ordinator with G3.1.
grantStages.understand: Article 3.1 assigns eleven responsibilities (a to k) to the Commitments Officer, from deciding on direct award to recovering funds.
grantStages.do: Have the Commitments Officer formally appoint the Co-ordinator with Template G3.1 and the Evaluation Committee with Template G13.1.
grantStages.check: Any delegation is in writing, to a cost centre manager in the same administrative entity, under Article 31 of the Financial Regulations.

sections.lead: The Commitments Officer decides, the Co-ordinator runs the procedure and the Evaluation Committee evaluates.
items: Responsible for every aspect of the procedure listed in Article 3.1.
A staff member responsible for the smooth running of the procedure, appointed with G3.1.
Evaluates proposals; appointed with G13.1 under Article 13.

sections.lead: Article 3.1 gives the Commitments Officer eleven responsibilities covering the procedure from start to finish.
items: Decide whether the direct award conditions of Article 2.1 are met; Article 9 sets the guarantees.
Approve the call, its publication means and submission arrangements, and ensure it complies with the Rule.
Formally appoint a staff member to plan and organise receipt and evaluation of applications (G3.1).
Appoint the Evaluation Committee, whose membership and prerogatives are set by Article 13 (G13.1).
Decide on the award under Articles 9.2, 14.5 and 14.7.
Inform applicants of the decision under Articles 14.8 and 14.9.
Sign the grant agreement, consulting DLAPIL on adapting the model to donor conditions or national law.
Decide not to publish certain results if, and only if, the grantee's vital interests are potentially threatened (Art. 2.1.4).
Suspend the agreement for unavoidable circumstances, political context or management reasons such as delays.
Terminate the agreement where difficulties make it necessary, after consulting DLAPIL.
Reduce grant amounts or recover them in full or in part, for instance where expenses are ineligible.

sections.lead: The department concerned prepares the call, and the Commitments Officer checks it before approval.
items: The call clearly specifies exclusion, eligibility and weighted award criteria, which cannot change after publication.
The call is published so as to achieve its objectives (Art. 8.2).
The call meets every requirement of Article 8.3.
sections.tip: Use the G8.3 quality control checklist as a communication tool between the Commitments Officer and the drafters.

sections.lead: The Commitments Officer may delegate the Article 3.1 responsibilities to a cost centre manager in his or her administrative entity.
must: Any delegation of Commitments Officer responsibilities must be in writing and follow Article 31 of the Financial Regulations.

grantStages.warning: Only the competent Commitments Officer, or a written delegate, may decide on direct award, the award decision, suspension, termination or recovery.
grantStages.best: Use the G8.3 checklist as a communication tool between the Commitments Officer and the drafters of the call.
checklist: Identify the competent Commitments Officer
Put any delegation in writing under Article 31
Appoint the Co-ordinator with Template G3.1
Appoint the Evaluation Committee with Template G13.1
Check the call against the G8.3 checklist before approval
Consult DLAPIL before terminating an agreement
templates: Call for proposals quality control checklist

grantStages.name: Criteria
grantStages.title: Exclusion, eligibility and award criteria
grantStages.lead: Each category of criteria has its own purpose: exclusion checks legal prerequisites, eligibility checks the applicant's capacity, award criteria evaluate the proposal itself.
grantStages.remember: Exclude, then check capacity, then score the proposal; never change criteria.
keyFacts: every award criterion, shown in the call
published criteria and weights are unalterable
grantStages.example: After publishing a call, the team realises one award criterion is weighted too heavily. Changing it would breach the unalterable character of criteria. Correct action: evaluate with the published weighting, or let the procedure end and launch a new call.
grantStages.understand: Criteria are applied in sequence: excluded applicants are not assessed further, and only eligible applicants are scored against weighted award criteria.
grantStages.do: Define clear exclusion grounds, threshold-based eligibility criteria and weighted award criteria, each with its supporting documents, in the call.
grantStages.check: Every criterion is reasonable, proportionate, relevant and verifiable, and every award criterion carries a published weighting.

sections.lead: Each category of criteria has its own purpose, and an applicant must pass each one before the next is applied.
items: Checks legal prerequisites, such as no criminal sentence linked to the applicant's activity.
Checks the applicant's capacity to implement the project.

sections.lead: Applicants who cannot guarantee compliance with the exclusion criteria are excluded and not assessed further.
must: The call must define the exclusion criteria.
Each applicant must sign a declaration on exclusion criteria at submission (G4.1.2A to G4.1.2E).
The grant agreement must oblige grantees to report any change of situation affecting the exclusion criteria for its full duration.

sections.lead: Eligibility criteria examine the applicant's capacity to implement the project, not the proposal itself.
items: The applicant's staff and human resources.
must: Each eligibility criterion must set a precise threshold; applicants below it are not examined against the award criteria.

sections.lead: Award criteria evaluate the proposal as such, and apply only to applicants who passed exclusion and eligibility.
must: Each award criterion must be relevant, verifiable and weighted.
The call must show the weighting of every award criterion and list the documents used to verify it.
sections.tip: Give each award criterion weighted sub-criteria so applicants understand what is required.

sections.lead: All criteria must be clearly formulated and founded on objective arguments.
items: Criteria must not unduly restrict access, nor be so specific or vague that they favour or disadvantage applicants.
Each criterion has a cause and effect link with the project's goals, which are defined first.
The call lists the documents used to verify each criterion, such as certified financial reports.

sections.lead: Published criteria are unalterable; this is a fundamental principle of Article 5.4.
must: Nobody may alter published criteria or their weighting, under any circumstances, for the entire duration of the procedure.

grantStages.warning: Once the call is published, no criterion or weighting may be changed for any reason; draft them carefully before approval.
grantStages.best: Define the project's goals first, then derive each eligibility criterion from them so the link is explicit.
checklist: Include the exclusion grounds and declaration template in the call
Set a measurable threshold for each eligibility criterion
Weight every award criterion and sub-criterion
List the supporting documents for every criterion
Test each criterion for relevance and proportionality
Add the change-of-situation clause to the agreement
templates: Declaration on exclusion criteria, BO or VC, natural person
Declaration on exclusion criteria, EU funds, natural person
Declaration on exclusion criteria, BO or VC, legal person
Declaration on exclusion criteria, EU funds, legal person
Declaration on exclusion criteria, EU funds, legal person, owners and executive officers

grantStages.name: Costs
grantStages.title: Eligible and ineligible costs
grantStages.lead: The grant ceiling is set on the basis of estimated eligible costs, which must meet seven conditions; certain costs are always ineligible.
grantStages.remember: Necessary, in budget, in period, on record; indirect costs max 7%.
grantStages.example: An applicant's budget includes buying an office building, interest on a loan and 10% overheads. Land and buildings and interest are ineligible, and indirect costs cannot exceed 7%. Correct action: remove both items and cap indirect costs at no more than 7%.
grantStages.understand: Only costs meeting all Article 6.2 conditions are eligible; indirect costs are capped at 7% and Article 7.1 lists costs that are never eligible.
grantStages.do: Build the estimated budget from eligible costs only and state the grant ceiling and any indirect cost rate in the agreement.
grantStages.check: Every budgeted cost appears in the estimated overall budget and falls within the implementation period defined to the day.

sections.lead: The maximum grant amount is based on the estimated eligible costs, which must meet Article 6.2.
must: The grant agreement must state the maximum amount of the grant.

sections.lead: A direct cost is eligible only if it meets all seven conditions of Article 6.2.
items: Strictly necessary for implementing the action, or for the grantee's operations in an operational grant.
Consistent with sound financial management, best value for money and cost-effectiveness.
Actually incurred by the grantee during the implementation period defined to the day in the agreement.
Recorded in the grantee's accounts under its applicable accounting standards.
Compliant with applicable tax and social security legislation.
Backed by originals or certified copies, certified generally by the grantee's treasurer.
Indicated in the estimated overall budget, including for operational grants.

sections.lead: Indirect costs may be eligible only if planned from the start, and never above 7% of the total.
must: The call must state the precise percentage of indirect costs, and the agreement must make it contractual.
Indirect costs must never exceed 7% of the total (Art. 6.3).

sections.lead: Article 7.1 lists eight costs that are never eligible, for reasons of principle or legal and financial certainty.
items: Expenditure financed by other sources (non-cumulative awards).
Debts and provisions for losses or debts incurred before the award.
Costs incurred outside the implementation period in the agreement.
Expenditure unrelated to the project or action.
Interest owed, which is never necessary to implement an action.
Purchase of land and buildings, completely excluded.
Currency exchange losses, which the grantee must guard against, for example with an account in a specific currency.
Loans to third parties, given the risks involved.

sections.lead: Renovation costs are excluded unless directly related to the project or action.
must: Where renovation is directly related to the action, the action description must specify its extent precisely.

sections.lead: The Article 7.1 list is not exhaustive and may be supplemented.
items: Extra items required by a donor of extra-budgetary resources.
Other requirements specific to the procedure in question.

grantStages.warning: Indirect costs may never exceed 7% of the total, and a cost not shown in the estimated budget cannot be eligible.
grantStages.best: Define the implementation period to the exact day in the agreement, since cost eligibility depends on it.
checklist: State the maximum grant amount in the agreement
Test each cost against conditions (a) to (g)
Cap indirect costs at 7% and publish the rate
Remove land purchases, interest, loans and exchange losses
Specify any project-related renovation in the action description
Add donor-specific ineligible costs where needed
templates: Guidelines for using grant agreement budget templates

grantStages.name: Call
grantStages.title: Drafting and publishing the call for proposals
grantStages.lead: A public call for proposals must reach the target public and contain everything applicants need to submit a complete application.
grantStages.remember: Objectives first; website always; answers for everyone.
keyFacts: call template for BO-VC / EU funds
grantStages.example: A call targets NGOs in one member state and is only on the Council website. The website is mandatory but not enough to reach that public. Correct action: add a local newspaper notice referring to the full call online and inform the Permanent Delegation.
grantStages.understand: Article 8.3 lists ten mandatory elements (a to j) of a call, and publication on the Organisation's website is an absolute prerequisite.
grantStages.do: Draft the call with G8.1A or G8.1B and the G8.2 application form, check it with G8.3, then publish it widely.
grantStages.check: All replies to questions are published to all potential applicants by the same means as the call.

sections.lead: Use the standard call and application form templates matching the funding source.
items: Call for proposals for the Ordinary Budget or Voluntary Contributions.
Call for proposals for EU funds.
Application form, used for all competitive procedures.
must: Drafters may adapt the application form but must keep the substance of Sections 1 to 3 and leave the declaration and signature in Sections 12 and 13 unchanged.

sections.lead: Article 8.3 lists ten elements that every call for proposals must contain.
items: The aims of the action; formulating them is the first stage of any procedure.
The required level of co-financing, preferably as a percentage of the estimated budget.
Ways to send proposals, supporting documents, deadline and the consequences of non-compliance.
A departmental address for written questions, with languages, question deadline and how replies are published.
When applicants will learn the outcome and when agreements should be signed.
The indicative timetable for implementing the action.
The criteria and the supporting documents each applicant must submit.
The criteria, their weighting and their supporting documents.
The number of potential grantees and the total value of the grants.
Terms based on the model: payment arrangements, any financial guarantees and any specific clauses.
sections.tip: Create a dedicated e-mail address for the procedure rather than using a staff member's personal address.

sections.lead: DLAPIL systematically verifies the submission arrangements when asked for a legal opinion on the draft call.
must: Drafters must agree any specific clause for the agreement with DLAPIL before it is published with the call.
sections.tip: Request a legal opinion before publication, especially where financial guarantees such as a deposit or bank guarantee are stipulated.

sections.lead: The means of publication must first and foremost reach the target public.
items: Mandatory, but not sufficient on its own.
A notice referring to the full call on the website, useful for calls limited to certain member states.
A useful extra channel, in wording suited to the procedure.
Informing them suits calls limited to one or several member states.
must: Every published document must comply with data protection rules.

sections.lead: Under non-discrimination, replies must reach all potential applicants, including those who did not ask.
items: Gather all questions into a single document.
Merge identical questions; omit irrelevant ones and those answered in the call.
Publish the document by the same means as the call.

grantStages.warning: Any specific clause to be added to the model agreement must be agreed with DLAPIL and published in the draft agreement with the call.
grantStages.best: Create a dedicated e-mail address for the procedure rather than using a staff member's personal address.
checklist: Formulate the objectives of the action first
Use G8.1A or G8.1B and the G8.2 application form
Cover all elements (a) to (j) of Article 8.3
Run the G8.3 quality control checklist
Request a DLAPIL legal opinion before publication
Publish on the website and through targeted channels
Publish one consolidated questions and answers document

Call for proposals for EU funds
Application form for BO or VC

grantStages.name: Submission
grantStages.title: Submission, receipt and opening of proposals
grantStages.lead: Submission conditions are strict and applied uniformly; proposals are opened only after the deadline, by the Co-ordinator with an Evaluation Committee member.
grantStages.remember: Never open early, never open alone, never alter a proposal.
keyFacts: Co-ordinator plus an Evaluation Committee member at opening
must be proved by the late applicant
grantStages.example: Ten proposals arrive and the Co-ordinator is keen to start before the deadline. Opening early would require cancelling the whole procedure. Correct action: wait for the deadline, open with a Committee member, number each proposal and record it in G11.1.
grantStages.understand: Opening proposals before the deadline, or altering their content after receipt, breaches transparency and non-discrimination.
grantStages.do: Open proposals after the deadline with an Evaluation Committee member present, number each one and record it in Template G11.1.
grantStages.check: Each proposal includes an estimated budget and information on other sources of financing.

sections.lead: Dispatch arrangements, closing date and supporting documents are strict requirements applied uniformly to all applicants.
must: The Co-ordinator must apply the consequences of non-compliance stated in the call stringently.

sections.lead: Whether a late proposal is examined depends on how the call certifies the dispatch date or time.
items: The postmark, delivery stamp or e-mail time decides whether a proposal was on time.
An applicant claiming unavoidable circumstances must prove force majeure.
Gives reasons in the draft report on exclusion and eligibility.
States in the consensus report whether force majeure is proven.
sections.tip: State in the call how the dispatch date and time are established.

sections.lead: The budget and funding information in each proposal make the key financial principles workable.
items: Used to assess feasibility, calculate co-financing and determine eligible expenditure.
Crucial for applying co-financing and non-cumulative awards.
must: Each proposal must include an estimated budget; costs outside it cannot be eligible.

sections.lead: For highly technical files, a concept note can test the fundamentals before shortlisted applicants submit a detailed proposal.
items: Checks the essential features of each proposal.
Shortlisted applicants develop the technical detail.
must: Unsuccessful applicants at either stage are informed only after the Commitments Officer's final award decision.
sections.tip: Avoid two stages for files with little technical content; decide case by case.

sections.lead: Data protection rules apply throughout the procedure, including implementation of the agreement.
must: The grant agreement must contain a clause on the conditions of publication of data; the model agreement includes one.

sections.lead: Proposals are opened only after the deadline, by two people, and recorded in Template G11.1.
items: Opening early should lead to cancellation of the whole procedure.
The Co-ordinator opens the proposals with a member of the Evaluation Committee.
Each proposal receives an identification number in the G11.1 report.
must: The Co-ordinator must never open proposals alone.
Nobody may alter the content of a proposal once the Secretariat has received it.

grantStages.warning: Never open proposals before the deadline or alone; either breach can require cancellation of the procedure.
grantStages.best: State in the call how the dispatch date and time are established, so late proposals can be decided objectively.
checklist: Apply submission conditions identically to every applicant
Keep proposals unopened until the deadline expires
Open proposals with an Evaluation Committee member present
Number each proposal and record it in G11.1
Check each proposal has a budget and funding information
Note late proposals and reasons for the draft report

grantStages.name: Eligibility Check
grantStages.title: Checking exclusion and eligibility; the Evaluation Committee
grantStages.lead: The Co-ordinator prepares a draft report on exclusion and eligibility for an Evaluation Committee whose members must be free of conflicts of interest.
grantStages.remember: Clarify, never improve: requests must not change a proposal's substance.
keyFacts: staff member on every Evaluation Committee
conflict of interest declaration, all members
grantStages.example: An applicant's financial statement page was badly scanned. This is a technical error, not a substantive change. Correct action: ask for that page only by a fixed date, and evaluate on available elements if it does not arrive.
grantStages.understand: The Co-ordinator checks signed exclusion declarations and eligibility thresholds; requests for information may clarify a proposal but never change its substance.
grantStages.do: Prepare the draft G14.1 report and send it with copies of all proposals to the Evaluation Committee members.
grantStages.check: Every Committee member has signed G13.4, and external members have also signed the G13.5 confidentiality declaration.

sections.lead: The Co-ordinator checks exclusion and eligibility and records the conclusions in a draft G14.1 report.
items: Confirm each applicant has duly signed the solemn declaration on exclusion criteria.
Verify each applicant meets every eligibility threshold.
Enter conclusions and comments in the draft G14.1 report.
Send the draft with a copy of all proposals to the Evaluation Committee members.

sections.lead: A request may clarify a proposal but never change its substance.
items: Allowed: details without effect on the outcome, such as personal data or an unselected option.
Allowed: a badly scanned page or a plainly outdated document version.
Not allowed: non-administrative additions are excluded and may trigger a fraud investigation.
must: The Co-ordinator must give the applicant a specified date; if nothing arrives, the evaluation proceeds on the elements available.
The Co-ordinator must ensure the process is transparent and non-discriminatory.

sections.lead: The Commitments Officer appoints the Evaluation Committee with Template G13.1.
must: Each Evaluation Committee must include at least one staff member.
sections.tip: Appoint a majority of staff members, ideally only staff; this is recommended but not binding.

sections.lead: Members from outside the Secretariat allow co-operation with donors or beneficiary state authorities and bring technical expertise.
must: External members must undertake in writing that they have no conflict of interest and will abide by the rules.
External members must sign the declaration of confidentiality (G13.5); staff are already bound by Article 26 of the Staff Regulations.

sections.lead: Each member undertakes on appointment to act in line with Article 13.3; the Vademecum (G13.2) explains the role.
items: Every member declares the absence of conflicts of interest.
Article 13.4 lists cases where a conflict is irrebuttably presumed.
The list is not exhaustive; other situations may also be conflicts.
must: A member in a presumed conflict of interest must withdraw or be excluded from the Committee.

grantStages.warning: A presumed conflict of interest under Article 13.4 cannot be rebutted; the member must withdraw or be excluded from the Committee.
grantStages.best: Appoint a Committee made up mainly or entirely of staff members to avoid disputes over interpreting the Rule.
checklist: Check every exclusion declaration is signed
Verify each eligibility threshold against the evidence
Limit information requests to clarifications with a fixed date
Collect G13.4 declarations from all Committee members
Collect G13.5 from members outside the Secretariat
Send the draft G14.1 report and all proposals to members

Declaration of absence of conflict of interests

grantStages.name: Evaluation
grantStages.title: Evaluating proposals and deciding the award
grantStages.lead: The Committee adopts the eligibility report, members score proposals individually, the Co-ordinator compiles a consensus report and the Commitments Officer decides.
grantStages.remember: Score 0–5, average equally, all sign, Commitments Officer reasons.
keyFacts: max calendar days to inform unsuccessful applicants
minimum enquiry period in the letter
grantStages.example: The consensus report for a media freedom call is signed by all members, but one recommended budget looks unreasonable. The Commitments Officer must verify cost, aims and available funds. Correct action: ask the Committee to amplify its report before adopting a reasoned G14.6 decision.
grantStages.understand: Members score each award criterion from 0 to 5 with comments; the consensus report averages scores equally and is adopted when all members sign.
grantStages.do: Run individual scoring with G14.3, compile the G14.4 consensus report and submit it for the Commitments Officer's reasoned G14.6 decision.
grantStages.check: Unsuccessful applicants are informed in writing no later than 15 calendar days after the successful ones.

sections.lead: Evaluation runs from the eligibility report to the Commitments Officer's reasoned decision.
items: The Committee adopts the exclusion and eligibility report, possibly by electronic consultation.
Each member completes G14.3 for each eligible proposal.
The Co-ordinator averages scores in the G14.4 consensus report.
All members sign the consensus report to adopt it.
The Commitments Officer adopts a reasoned G14.6 decision.
must: The Co-ordinator must keep a paper or electronic copy of any electronic consultation.
Only applicants declared eligible may be evaluated against the award criteria.

sections.lead: Each member scores every award criterion or sub-criterion from 0 to 5, with coherent explanatory comments.
items: Fails the criterion or cannot be assessed because information is missing.
Approached superficially or with intrinsic weaknesses.
Generally meets the criterion but with intrinsic weaknesses.
Largely meets the criterion despite some shortcomings.
Very largely meets the criterion with few shortcomings.
Fulfils every aspect; any shortcomings are minor.

sections.lead: The Co-ordinator averages the scores, giving equal weight to each evaluator, in the G14.4 consensus report.
items: The total amount of funds concerned by the procedure.
The list of successful applicants and selected proposals.
must: All Committee members must sign the consensus report before it is adopted.
sections.tip: If scores diverge too widely, talk to the evaluators or convene the Committee to reach a common position.

sections.lead: The Commitments Officer must give reasons, for example by endorsing the attached consensus report without reservation (G14.6).
items: The selected project pursues the aims stated in the call.
The project's cost and content appear reasonable.
Funds are available to finance the project.
must: The Commitments Officer must decide only on a reasoned and documented consensus report, and ask the Committee to amend or amplify it otherwise.

sections.lead: After an unsuccessful call the Commitments Officer may award no grant or launch a new call, recorded in Template G14.7A.
items: The Commitments Officer may decide without prior action by the Committee.
The Commitments Officer decides only after the Committee has analysed the proposals.

sections.lead: The Commitments Officer informs all applicants of the outcome in writing.
items: Inform promptly; the Rule sets no deadline.
Within 15 calendar days of the successful applicants.
Within 15 calendar days of the successful applicants.
must: The Commitments Officer must inform unsuccessful applicants no later than 15 calendar days after the successful ones.
Each letter to an unsuccessful applicant must explain how to enquire and give a cut-off date of at least 7 calendar days.
sections.tip: Inform all applicants on the same day and direct their questions to the Co-ordinator.

grantStages.warning: The 15 calendar day deadline for informing unsuccessful applicants is imperative, and the letter must state a cut-off date for enquiries of at least 7 calendar days.
grantStages.best: Send all successful and unsuccessful letters on the same day and direct questions to the Co-ordinator.
checklist: Adopt the G14.1 report and keep a record of exchanges
Collect a completed G14.3 sheet per member per proposal
Average scores equally in the G14.4 consensus report
Have every Committee member sign the consensus report
Obtain the Commitments Officer's reasoned G14.6 decision
Send G14.8 and G14.9A or G14.9B letters on time

Letter to unsuccessful applicants (exclusion or ineligibility)

grantStages.name: Complaints
grantStages.title: Enquiries, complaints and allegations
grantStages.lead: Unsuccessful applicants must first enquire, may then complain within 30 calendar days, and complaints go to the Co-ordinator and, failing a manifest error, to the Review Board.
grantStages.remember: Enquire first, complain within 30 days, about the evaluation only.
keyFacts: calendar days to lodge a complaint after the enquiry reply
for the Review Board to meet after receipt
Review Board members: Auditor, DLAPIL, Treasurer
grantStages.example: An unsuccessful NGO complains that its complete proposal was rejected as incomplete. That is a manifest error. Correct action: the Co-ordinator alerts the Evaluation Committee, which reassesses and recommends measures to the Commitments Officer.
grantStages.understand: A complaint is admissible only if it contests how the proposal was examined; it cannot challenge the wording of the criteria unless they breach Article 2.
grantStages.do: Reply to enquiries in writing with G15.2, screen complaints for manifest error and transmit the rest to the Review Board without delay.
grantStages.check: Time limits are counted in calendar days from midnight after the triggering act, extended to the next working day if needed.

sections.lead: An unsuccessful applicant enquires first, may then complain, and the complaint is screened before any Review Board.
items: The applicant asks in writing why it was not selected.
The Co-ordinator replies in writing with G15.2.
The applicant complains within 30 calendar days of the reply.
The Co-ordinator screens the complaint immediately.
Without a manifest error, the Board examines the complaint.
The Commitments Officer decides on measures (G15.7B).

sections.lead: Reasons for non-selection are given promptly and in writing, not by telephone.
items: Which complaints will not be accepted.
must: The Co-ordinator must check that each enquiry arrived within the deadline (at least 7 days) stated in the letter.
The G15.2 reply must explain the complaint procedure and state the address for complaints.

sections.lead: A complaint is admissible only if it contests how the proposal was examined.
items: An enquiry must precede the complaint.
Within 30 calendar days of notification of the reply to the enquiry.
The call reference and the proposal's identification number.
Full particulars of the grievances and all necessary documents.
must: The Co-ordinator must declare inadmissible (G15.3A) any complaint about the wording of criteria, unless they breach Article 2.
The Co-ordinator must request missing documents in writing (G15.3B) within a stated reasonable time.

sections.lead: Time limits run in calendar days from midnight on the day after the triggering act.
items: A reply notified at 11 am on the 2nd starts the clock at midnight on the 3rd.
Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays count.
A deadline falling on a non-working day moves to the next working day.

sections.lead: A manifest error is a gross or clear error in interpreting the facts or in the procedure, such as rejecting a complete proposal as incomplete.
items: Examines the complaint immediately and alerts the Committee if an error is found.
Reassesses the proposal and recommends measures.
Decides the measures to redress the error.

sections.lead: Without a manifest error, the complaint goes to a Review Board that checks the evaluation but cannot redo it.
items: Representatives of the internal Auditor, the Director of Legal Advice and Public International Law and the Treasurer, none involved in the evaluation.
Meets within 30 calendar days of receiving the complaint.
Checks that criteria were applied coherently and without discrimination.
May recommend a fresh evaluation by reasoned opinion (G15.7A); the Commitments Officer decides (G15.7B).
must: The Co-ordinator must send the complaint and all evaluation documents to the Review Board without delay.

sections.lead: The complaints procedure only reviews evaluation errors and is not an inquiry into misconduct.
items: May receive allegations of fraud, corruption or misconduct.
May receive the same allegations and acts under Rule 1327.

grantStages.warning: Complaints contesting anything other than the examination of the proposal are inadmissible, and the Review Board may not substitute its own evaluation.
grantStages.best: Keep every evaluation document on file so the complete record can be sent to the Review Board at once.
checklist: Check enquiries were received within the stated deadline
Reply to enquiries in writing using G15.2
Confirm an enquiry preceded the complaint
Check admissibility and completeness of the complaint
Screen the complaint for manifest error immediately
Transmit the full file to the Review Board without delay
Refer fraud allegations to the internal Auditor or DGA

grantStages.name: Agreement
grantStages.title: Drafting, signing and amending the grant agreement
grantStages.lead: A written grant agreement is imperative; it is based on the DLAPIL model but must be adapted to the context, the proposal and the donor's requirements.
grantStages.remember: Always in writing; amend management details, never the total amount.
keyFacts: model agreement for BO-VC / EU funds
grantStages.example: A grantee asks to change its bank details and add €5,000 to the grant. Bank details are a management matter, but the total amount must not increase. Correct action: amend the bank details in writing with G17.3 or e-mail and refuse the increase.
grantStages.understand: The agreement must contain a description of the action, an estimated budget, the implementation period, reporting obligations and a limit on third-party liability.
grantStages.do: Adapt Template G17.2A or G17.2B with its annexes, consulting DLAPIL where needed, and have the Commitments Officer sign it.
grantStages.check: The estimated budget total equals the grant amount and the implementation period does not pre-date the proposal deadline.

sections.lead: A verbal agreement not put into writing is contrary to the Rule.
must: The parties must sign a written grant agreement.

sections.lead: The DLAPIL model is only a basis and must be adapted to the context, the proposal and any donor requirements.
items: Agreement for the Ordinary Budget or Voluntary Contributions.
Guidance on how to prepare an agreement.
must: An agreement financed by extra-budgetary resources must reflect the donor's requirements, notably on visibility and eligibility of costs.
sections.tip: Consult DLAPIL for a legal opinion on the terms.

sections.lead: Every agreement, including for operational grants, sets out the action, the budget, the grantee's obligations and the implementation period.
items: Preferably in an annex, including any purchases or sub-grants the grantee will make.
Itemised in an annex (G17.2D), with a total equal to the grant amount.
Narrative and financial reporting, using model reports (G17.2E or G17.2F).
Defined precisely, since cost eligibility depends on it.
must: The implementation period must never pre-date the deadline for proposals.
sections.tip: Use the budget annex structure as the framework for financial reporting.

sections.lead: An amendment can use any written format that unambiguously shows both parties' consent.
items: Obtain the authorised staff member's agreement first and copy him or her; list the change and ask the grantee to confirm by return.
Both parties sign a document (G17.3) setting out the change.
Management matters such as deadlines, contact details or bank details.
Any increase in the total grant amount or change that distorts the initial conditions.
must: Every amendment must reference the agreement and state which provisions are supplemented or cancelled and replaced.

sections.lead: The model agreement G17.2A already limits the Organisation's third-party liability.
must: Every grant agreement must contractually limit the Organisation's third-party liability.

sections.lead: Grants implemented in Ukraine need an extra security and safety document.
items: Annex V on security and safety.

grantStages.warning: An amendment must never increase the total grant amount or alter conditions in a way that creates unequal treatment between applicants.
grantStages.best: Use the estimated budget annex structure as the framework for the grantee's financial reporting.
checklist: Choose G17.2A or G17.2B according to the funding source
Attach the action description and G17.2D budget annex
Match the budget total to the grant amount
Define the implementation period without retroactivity
Set narrative and financial reporting obligations
Keep the third-party liability limitation clause
Record amendments in writing with G17.3 or e-mail

How to prepare a grant agreement
Annex V, security and safety for grants in Ukraine
Addendum on security and safety in Ukraine

grantStages.name: Filing
grantStages.title: Record-keeping, interpretation and templates
grantStages.lead: The initiating department keeps the complete file, the Rule is interpreted in good faith, and the templates must be completed and cleaned before use.
grantStages.remember: Keep everything, from Co-ordinator appointment to final supporting documents.
keyFacts: options and comments to delete before sending

grantStages.do: File every procedure document in line with your entity's document management table and finalise templates before sending them.
grantStages.check: Comments, blue highlighting and bracketed [XX] options have been removed from every template sent to third parties.

sections.lead: The department that initiated the procedure keeps the complete grant file.
items: Validation of the supporting documents certifying proper use of the grant.
must: Each entity's document management table must reflect this record-keeping requirement.

sections.lead: The Rule is interpreted in good faith under Article 19, keeping in mind its spirit and the principles in its Preamble.

sections.tip: Use the guide and its appendices for all award procedures; misuse may lead to an administrative inquiry.

Delete comments, blue highlighting and bracketed [XX] options.
Parts for the applicant or grantee are marked in red.

Include supporting documents validating use of the grant
Align filing with the document management table
