payment-file.lead: Continue the control trail from the PO stage and build a finance-ready payment file.
payment-file.remember: Pay only for completed, accepted work that matches the approved contractual basis.
payment-file.understand: A payment closes the trail opened at PO stage, so it must match the same contract, supplier and approval route.
payment-file.do: Confirm completion with a signed Certificate of Acceptance of Work or Payment Request Memorandum, match the invoice to the PO and contract, complete the PMM synopsis and obtain CCM approval before the file goes to the Treasurer.
payment-file.check: The payment file is complete, the ACCM has recorded the CCM approval, discrepancies are resolved and the payment evidence is archived until settlement.
figures: The default payment term is 60 days from receipt of the invoice or execution, whichever is later, unless the contract sets other terms.

year-end.title: Year-end closing
year-end.lead: Check delivery dates, complete payment files, follow up suppliers and finalise POs when the expenditure is fully recorded.
year-end.remember: Only delivery by 31 December 2026 counts as 2026 expenditure.
year-end.understand: Expenditure must be charged to the financial year in which the goods were delivered or the services were rendered.
year-end.do: Review open POs, follow up suppliers for missing invoices and send complete payment files to Finance as soon as they are ready.
year-end.check: All 2026 expenditure is recorded in FIMS and the Fiche PO shows it under Amount billed or Invoices before the PO is finalised.
figures: Only goods delivered and services rendered by 31 December 2026 can be included in 2026 expenditure.

petty-cash.title: Petty cash
petty-cash.lead: Use petty cash only for small-value operational needs, within the authorised limit, with a clear supporting file.
petty-cash.remember: Get CCM approval before spending, and keep each invoice paid by petty cash at or below €50.
petty-cash.understand: Petty cash is a small-value exception, so it must not replace the normal procurement or payment route.
petty-cash.do: Check each invoice against the €50 limit, obtain CCM approval, let the ACCM issue the PO and send the request to DPFL, which transfers the approved amount to a local bank account.
petty-cash.check: Every cash advance has a signed cash transfer form, cash is kept in a lockable box, and each invoice is supported by evidence of its link to the project, such as the activity, date and place, or for taxis the traveller, purpose and why public transport was not used.
figures: Invoices paid by petty cash must not exceed €50 each; above that, use the normal purchasing and payment route.
Every staff member who receives a cash advance signs a cash transfer form and keeps the cash in a lockable box.

filing.title: Filing and audit trail
filing.lead: Keep project, procurement and financial records easy to find, easy to verify and ready for review.
filing.remember: Store every approval and document with the transaction it supports.
filing.understand: A complete and traceable file shows why each action was taken, who approved it and how it was executed.
filing.do: File decision, approval and execution evidence in the DMS project folder, using clear names, dates and references, and keep project documentation electronically and physically.
filing.check: Final PDF evidence and its editable source are kept together and every file can be found and verified.
figures: Project documentation, including deliverables and supporting documents, must remain easy to retrieve for audit for ten years after the end of the project.

foma.title: FOMA workflows
foma.lead: Controlled handover workflows and financial guidance for day-to-day field-office operations.
foma.remember: Each file moves to the next role only after its control is complete.
foma.understand: Field-office files pass between the requester or Project Team, ACCM, RFO and CCM, and each role has its own control.
foma.do: Choose the workflow, complete your stage and hand the file over to the next role in the route.
foma.check: Each stage has been controlled and the file has reached the final validation or the donor route where required.

foma/reports.title: Financial reporting
foma/reports.lead: Prepare and reconcile the project's current financial position and retain a controlled reporting package.
foma/reports.remember: Reconcile spent and committed figures to the source data before finalising.
foma/reports.understand: The financial report gives a clear and traceable picture of the project's current financial position for review and validation.
foma/reports.do: Build the report from the correct data, reconcile it, apply the JP or VC structure and complete the reporting controls.
foma/reports.check: No unexplained discrepancy, broken formula or unsupported figure remains, and the final report is archived with its evidence.
figures: At least once per year, the report should include actual and forecast expenditure for the coming year.

foma/forecast.title: Forecast and budget revision
foma/forecast.lead: Plan future expenditure, revise the budget and identify the applicable route.
foma/forecast.remember: Assess the ±25% threshold per Budget Heading, not the project total.
foma/forecast.understand: The size of each Budget Heading variation and any contractual change decide whether a revision follows the Notification or Addendum route.
foma/forecast.do: Prepare the FORECAST working sheet, collect the Project Team input, then review the variations and decide the route.
foma/forecast.check: Formulas are intact, the Project Team input is consistent and the route decision is documented.
figures: For a Joint Programme, a variation within ±25% at Budget Heading level follows Notification, and a variation above ±25% follows Addendum.

foma/addendum.title: Addendum workflow
foma/addendum.lead: Prepare a Joint Programme Addendum package from the latest financial report and forecast.
foma/addendum.remember: Changes to total cost, duration or scope always require an Addendum.
foma/addendum.understand: An Addendum amends the donor-approved contractual budget, so it needs a clean, validated and justified package.
foma/addendum.do: Confirm the route, prepare the revised budget, collect the Project Team justification and build the clean donor package.
foma/addendum.check: The Addendum is signed by both parties, the revised budget is uploaded to PMM and all project records are aligned.
figures: Where any relevant Budget Heading of a Joint Programme exceeds ±25%, the Addendum route applies.

vat.title: VAT procedures
vat.lead: Clarify VAT before signature, check it at PO and invoice stage, and keep the VAT trail.
vat.remember: Clarify VAT before signing the contract or order form.
vat.understand: VAT exemption is a privilege of the Council of Europe, and staff must follow the procedures carefully and meet the deadlines for requesting exemption certificates.
vat.do: Establish the supplier's VAT status and place of taxation, request any exemption certificate through MSA form 9215 within the deadlines, check the invoice particulars and pay to the contractual bank account.
vat.check: The invoice matches the agreed VAT treatment and the VAT correspondence is filed in the DMS with the invoice and payment evidence.
figures: All requests for VAT exemption certificates go through MSA form 9215 and its SLA, which help departments submit correct files and limit the risk of rejection by the French authorities.
A single card purchase is limited to €5,000, and card payments remain exceptions.
The Organisation-wide monthly card limit is €30,000; larger amounts should preferably be paid by transfer.
The default payment term is 60 days from receipt of the invoice or execution, whichever is later, unless the contract sets other terms.

events.title: Events and GDD
events.lead: Manage event finance from the call-off to the payment file, including budget reconciliation and exchange-rate evidence.
events.remember: Document every budget change and keep CCM approval for significant ones.
events.understand: The final event budget often differs from the initial one, so each change must be explained and supported in the payment file.
events.do: Run the call-off, submit the Event Management PO, collect delivery evidence and compare the final budget with the initial one.
events.check: The payment file holds the signed final budget, CCM approval e-mails for significant changes and exchange-rate evidence where needed.

contractTypes.name: One-off contract
contractTypes.useWhen: The need is quantifiable and definable and very unlikely to recur.
contractTypes.suppliers: One supplier, which may be a consortium; the contract may be split into lots.
contractTypes.ordering: No orders: price, specifications and quantities are fixed in the contract.
contractTypes.duration: Until both parties have completed their obligations; a delivery deadline per deliverable; cannot be renewed.
contractTypes.control: The CCM signs, as it is a legal and financial commitment; repeated one-off contracts for the same need are prohibited artificial splitting.

contractTypes.name: Framework contract
contractTypes.useWhen: The need can be defined as units and recurs often but cannot be fully quantified.
contractTypes.suppliers: One supplier (simple) or several (multiple), using ranking for goods and general services or pooling for intellectual services.
contractTypes.ordering: The buyer entity issues order forms at the fixed unit prices, with concrete deliverables, a deadline and a lump-sum price; the Council is not obliged to buy.
contractTypes.duration: No minimum; no more than four years, or five exceptionally; no order after the end date.
contractTypes.control: The CCM signs each order after the PO is raised; pooling choices are justified in a note approved by the CCM; spending under a competitive bidding framework contract must not exceed €184,000.

contractTypes.name: Framework agreement
contractTypes.useWhen: The need is regular but variable, uncertain or complex.
contractTypes.suppliers: At least three suppliers per lot, selected on competence without price competition.
contractTypes.ordering: Each need goes to a call-off (mini-competition) among the pool, evaluated on the published award criteria.
contractTypes.duration: No minimum; no more than four years, or five exceptionally; call-offs only during validity.
contractTypes.control: The CCM approves and signs each call-off; call-offs above €184,000 go to the Tenders Board; rarely recommended below €184,000 in total.

limits.rule: Direct award allowed up to this amount for goods, general services and works; competitive bidding above it.
Direct award allowed up to this amount for intellectual services; competitive bidding above it.
Below this amount excluding VAT, a competitive bidding purchase may compare the public prices of three or more suppliers (Article 21.2); screenshots archived.
From this amount to €184,000, extrabudgetary-funded competitive bidding and exceptional direct awards need a Legal Compliance Review; e-procurement mandatory above it from 1 April 2026.
Above this amount, an international public call for tenders is required; exceptional direct awards and call-offs from this value go to the Tenders Board.
Maximum bank card payment per purchase, and per month for the whole Organisation.
Call-off amendments up to 10% of the original value need CCM authorisation; above 10%, consult DLAPIL.
After three call-offs with all tenders more than 20% above market price, the Council may tender outside the framework agreement.
Minimum invitees in competitive bidding (nine for a multiple framework contract with a pool of three); minimum pool per lot in a framework agreement.
Maximum duration of framework contracts, framework agreements and multi-year contracts.
Minimum publication period for an international call.
No answers to questions later than 48 hours before the deadline; minimum time for Tenders Board members to approve a request.
Response time of the DGA Procurement Unit at procurement@coe.int.
DLAPIL processing time for a complete Legal Compliance Review request.
Offers remain valid for 180 calendar days from the deadline.
Unsuccessful bidders are notified in writing within 15 days, after the contract is signed.
Deadline for an unsuccessful bidder's enquiry after notification.
Deadline for a complaint to the Tenders Board, which replies within 30 days; also the deadline for an appeal to an ad hoc review board in international calls.
Ad hoc review board reply time; also the default payment term from invoice or execution, whichever is later.
Usual notice period to object to tacit renewal, never less than one month.
Usual maximum time an order or call-off may continue after the framework end date.
Optional exclusion of suppliers that failed a Council contract in the previous three years.
Retention period for all contract and tender documents.
Annual declaration of interests, or within one month of a change.

roles.name: Buyer entity
roles.does: Runs the whole process, from forecasting the need to executing the contract; drafts documents, invites, assesses and manages the contract.

roles.name: Authorised staff members
roles.does: Open offers, assess offers and negotiate, as designated in writing by the CO or CCM.

roles.name: Commitments Officer (CO)
roles.does: Authorises expenditure, approves budget-line forecasts and usually delegates to CCMs.

roles.name: Commitments Control Manager (CCM)
roles.does: Validates the choice of procedure, tender files, awards, contracts, orders, call-offs and amendments.

roles.name: Tenders Board
roles.does: Authorises and validates international calls, and is consulted on negotiations, amendments and direct awards.

roles.name: Tenders Board Secretariat
roles.does: Checks files, forwards requests, publishes international calls and opens e-mailed offers.

roles.name: DLAPIL
roles.does: Handles legal questions, templates and training, and performs the Legal Compliance Review.
roles.when: Always for legal issues; LCR for extrabudgetary €55,000 to €184,000

roles.name: DGA Procurement Unit
roles.does: Gives non-legal support: market analysis, sourcing, e-procurement, templates and KPIs.

roles.name: TPA
roles.does: Registers suppliers in FIMS, provides card numbers and pays invoices.

roles.name: DPC
roles.does: Co-ordinates programming and extrabudgetary resources for co-operation projects.

roles.name: DIO
roles.does: Audits, evaluates and investigates; receives reports of suspected fraud.

roles.name: Specialist directorates (DIT, DC, DGS, ITEM)
roles.does: Approve or advise on IT, communication, works and multimedia purchases.

howTo.title: How to request a Legal Compliance Review
steps: Buyer entity: submit the DLAPIL request form titled Request for LCR.
Buyer entity: attach the direct award memorandum or all tender documents.
Buyer entity: state the procedure, estimated total expenditure, funding source and entities already consulted.
DLAPIL: process the complete request within 5 working days and give its visa in writing.
CCM: approve the launch once the visa is received.

howTo.title: How to submit to the Tenders Board
howTo.who: CCM, Tenders Board Secretariat, Tenders Board, buyer entity
steps: CCM: e-mail the tender documents and an explanatory memo to the Tenders Board Secretariat.
Tenders Board Secretariat: forward to members, allowing at least 48 hours, on the Tenders Board SharePoint.
Buyer entity: answer members' questions on the SharePoint.
Tenders Board: post its decision on the SharePoint and send it by e-mail or e-procurement.
Buyer entity: make any requested changes and send the updated version to the Secretariat for final validation.

howTo.title: How to open offers
howTo.who: Authorised staff members, Tenders Board Secretariat
steps: Wait until the submission deadline has passed.
With e-procurement: one authorised staff member of the buyer entity opens the offers, which unlock automatically.
Competitive bidding by e-mail: at least two authorised staff members of the buyer entity open the offers.
International call by e-mail: the Tenders Board Secretariat opens offers sent to cdm@coe.int with an authorised member of the buyer entity.
Those opening record and confirm receipt and prices.

howTo.title: How to review and sign a contract
steps: Buyer entity: check that the documents are correct, reflect negotiations and have not been modified by the supplier.
Buyer entity: check that the act of engagement is complete and signed by the supplier.
Buyer entity: for a new supplier, submit MSA 4002 so that TPA creates the supplier in FIMS.
Buyer entity: raise the purchase order in FIMS.
CCM: countersign with a wet-ink or electronic signature.
Buyer entity: send a signed PDF copy to the supplier and archive the documents.

howTo.title: How to amend a contract
steps: Buyer entity: obtain the CCM's written agreement before proceeding.
Buyer entity: send the supplier an e-mail (CCM in copy) or a document naming the contract and the provisions supplemented or replaced, using the standard wording.
Supplier: confirm by return e-mail or sign the document.
Buyer entity: for call-off increases above 10%, seek DLAPIL advice first.

howTo.title: How to place an order under a framework contract
steps: Buyer entity: identify the supplier using the ranking or pooling rules.
Buyer entity: complete the order form with deliverables, deadline, lump-sum price, project ID, FC number and VAT regime, and raise the PO.
Supplier: sign the order form and return a scanned copy.
CCM: countersign, adding the PO number and any advance payment percentage.
Buyer entity: send the signed copy to the supplier; the order is then binding.

howTo.title: How to launch a call-off under a framework agreement
steps: Buyer entity: prepare terms of reference and a deadline; the CCM approves before publication.
Buyer entity: send it to the preselected suppliers without revealing the others' identities.
Buyer entity: evaluate tenders on the published award criteria; late tenders are not considered.
Tenders Board: approve any call-off above €184,000.
CCM: sign the call-off after the VAT requirements are entered.

howTo.title: How to inform bidders of the outcome
steps: Inform the successful bidder in writing.
Sign the contract.
Notify unsuccessful bidders in writing within 15 days with the reason and the Article 24 enquiry procedure.
Disclose only the winner's amount, name and country.

Contractual document signed by the supplier/consultant, used with the Order Form (e.g. for direct awards).
Approved plan of activities. Once approved, it allows limited flexibility above the activity budget; it should cover the implementation period and be reviewed periodically.
The part of a split 2026–2027 service charged to the next year under the year-end allocation table.
Exercises expenditure and procurement approval within the applicable delegation; validates POs, authorises negotiation in competitive bidding, approves petty cash before spending.
Provides the Legal Compliance Review required before CCM approval for extrabudgetary or mixed funding from €55,000 to below €184,000, and advises on changes to legal contractual clauses.
Where the project file is organised: contract documents, activities, POs, signed and editable versions together.
Pool of preselected suppliers; each specific need is awarded through a mini-competition (call-off). Generally up to 4 years.
Recurring need with definable units and fixed unit prices; orders are placed with order forms. Generally up to 4 years.
System where expenditure is recorded; check “Amount billed” / “Invoices” on the Fiche PO before finalising a PO.
Jointly funded programme. A Budget Heading variation above ±25%, or a change in total cost, duration or scope, requires an Addendum.
Organisation's regular budget. Petty cash invoices may not exceed €50 each.
Financial commitment. No activity should start until the PO is opened, signatures are collected and the provider holds the countersigned documents.
Specification of the requirement: context, objective, deliverables, timing and technical requirements.
Voluntary funding; budget revisions follow the VC route, with donor acceptance where funding is earmarked.
Funding outside the Ordinary Budget. From €55,000 it adds a Legal Compliance Review before CCM approval.
Contractual revision of a JP budget/agreement requiring external acceptance before implementation.
JP budget change route where every relevant Budget Heading stays within ±25% and no contractual element changes.
Grouping of budget lines (e.g. 1 Human resources, 2 Travel). The ±25% test is applied at this level, not to the project total.
Authorises launch, negotiation and award for international public calls for tenders (≥ €184,000).
